> detection, and the interaction states.**

- The **application** declares a theme: token overrides (base values = the
  **light** design, `dark.`-prefixed values = the **dark** design) and, in a
  style property, a **token reference** instead of a literal value.
- The **renderer** supplies platform-appropriate defaults for the standard
  catalog (both light and dark), derives the **effective color scheme** from the
  platform (OS / browser / native theme), resolves token references, and owns
  hover/pressed/focus/disabled styling.

This preserves native look-and-feel by default and gives the application
cross-renderer consistency when it overrides tokens.

### Ownership

| Aspect | Owner |
|--------|-------|
| Theme values (base + `dark.*`) | Application |
| Color-scheme detection (light/dark) | Renderer (platform-derived; app may force via `SET_COLOR_SCHEME`) |
| Default token values (light + dark) | Renderer |
| Token resolution (override → default → parent → fallback) | Renderer |
| Interaction states (hover/pressed/focus/disabled) | Renderer |
| Literal property values | Application |

## Token Identification

Tokens are identified by **dot-separated string paths** — `color.primary`,
`font.body.size`, `space.2` — case-sensitive, lowercase recommended. A `dark.`
prefix selects the **dark variant** of a token (`dark.color.primary`).

The path namespace is **open**: the standard catalog below is a contract the
renderer MUST implement; any path outside it is **application-defined** and
renderer-optional (the renderer falls back rather than erroring).

A token's value uses the standard [value types](./OPCODE.md#value-types) —

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `color.primary` | Primary brand / accent fill |
| `color.secondary` | Secondary brand / accent fill |
| `color.background` | Document / canvas background |
| `color.surface` | Raised surface (cards, panels, popovers) |
| `color.text.primary` | Primary text color |
| `color.text.secondary` | Secondary / muted text color |
| `color.text.onPrimary` | Text placed on a `color.primary` fill |
| `color.border` | Default border / outline color |
| `color.accent` | Accent for controls (focus, selection, toggle fill) |

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `font.body.size` | Body text size |
| `font.body.weight` | Body text weight (100–900) |
| `font.body.family` | Body font family (STRING) |

its own via the `font.<style>.*` token paths above, or set an explicit

multiplied by an arbitrary number.

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `space.base` | The spacing **unit** (F32) — override this to change the whole density |
| `space.<N>` | `space.base` × N, where N is any positive decimal (`space.1`, `space.2`, `space.0.5`, `space.3.75`) — **computed** by the resolver |

   renderer resolves `space.base` and multiplies by the numeric leaf. Individual
   members MUST NOT be overridden via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` — override `space.base`

   is `dark.space.base`).

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `border.width.thin` | Default hairline/border width |

Tier 2: `border.width.thick`.

Shadows are composite; each component is its own token:

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `elevation.low.color` / `radius` / `x` / `y` / `blur` | Low elevation shadow |
| `elevation.high.color` / `radius` / `x` / `y` / `blur` | High elevation shadow |

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `opacity.disabled` | The renderer MAY apply this to disabled controls. The disabled **state** itself is the `ENABLED` property; its visual handling (including this opacity) remains renderer-owned. |

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `control.background` | Control resting background |
| `control.foreground` | Control content (label/icon) color |
| `control.border` | Control border color |
| `control.border.width` | Control border width |
| `control.radius` | Control corner radius |
| `control.padding.horizontal` / `control.padding.vertical` | Control inner padding |
| `control.height` | Control height (F32) |
| `control.font.size` / `control.font.weight` | Control text |

**Slider** (Tier 1): `slider.accent`, `slider.track`, `slider.thumb`.

**Picker** (Tier 2): `picker.accent`, `picker.background`, `picker.border`,

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, 'docs/**', 'feature/**', 'fix/**', 'spec/**']
  pull_request:

jobs:
  rust:
    name: Rust (workspace + C ABI + no_std/wasm)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # The workspace includes pathland-render-gtk (GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer)
      # and pathland-render-qt (Qt Quick), so the runner needs the GTK4,
      # libadwaita, GStreamer, and Qt system libraries before `cargo test` can
      # link them. GStreamer is required because the GTK renderer plays app-driven
      # media through a direct GStreamer playbin (GTK4's own media backend is
      # compiled out of some builds); the plugins are the runtime set the audio
      # stack uses (playbin, volume/audioconvert, mp3 decode). The Qt libraries
      # are installed in the next step.
      - name: Install GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libgtk-4-dev \
            libadwaita-1-dev \
            libglib2.0-dev \
            libcairo2-dev \
            libpango1.0-dev \
            libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-dev \
            libgraphene-1.0-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev \
            gstreamer1.0-plugins-base \
            gstreamer1.0-plugins-good \
            gstreamer1.0-libav

      - name: Install Qt6 (QML/Quick) system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            qt6-base-dev \
            qt6-declarative-dev \
            qt6-declarative-private-dev \
            qt6-multimedia-dev \
            qml6-module-qtqml \
            qml6-module-qtqml-models \
            qml6-module-qtqml-workerscript \
            qml6-module-qtquick \
            qml6-module-qtquick-layouts \
            qml6-module-qtquick-controls \
            qml6-module-qtquick-templates \
            qml6-module-qtquick-window \
            qml6-module-qtmultimedia
        # The dev headers alone don't ship the QML runtime modules; the Qt
        # renderer's offscreen tests instantiate the QML (QtQml + WorkerScript,
        # Items, stacks/Grid via QtQuick.Layouts, Qt Quick Controls, Multimedia)
        # through QQmlComponent, so the qml6-module-* runtime files are required
        # too. Note the Qt6 package names: `-window` (the Qt5 `-window2` name
        # does not exist), and private headers need qt6-declarative-private-dev.

      - name: Install Rust (stable + wasm32 target)
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown

      - name: Cache cargo
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: lib/rust -> target

      - name: Test workspace
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo test

      - name: Qt renderer headless smoke
        working-directory: lib/rust
        env:
          QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen
          QT_QUICK_BACKEND: software
        run: cargo test -p pathland-render-qt

      # The DOM renderer's constants/token conventions and the cross-renderer SSR
      # golden fixtures are GENERATED from Rust (pathland-ts-codegen /
      # pathland-html-golden). Regenerate them here and fail if the committed
      # files drifted — so a renumbered constant or a changed SSR shape can't land
      # without its TS/fixture counterparts.
      - name: Verify generated TS + golden fixtures are current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen
          cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit
          git diff --exit-code -- \
            lib/typescript/src/constants.ts \
            lib/typescript/src/generated \
            lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr

      - name: Build the C ABI (cdylib, used by the Java JNA ring interop / native hosts)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-core-capi

      - name: no_std / wasm32 direction guard
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: ./check-wasm.sh

      # The Java HTML renderer shim needs the Rust renderer cdylib (the jar embeds
      # it so it travels with the artifact). Build it here and hand it to the java
      # job via an artifact.
      - name: Build the HTML renderer cdylib
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-render-html

      - name: Upload the renderer dylib for the java job
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html.so
          retention-days: 1

  java:
    name: Java (Maven reactor, JDK ${{ matrix.java }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [rust]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        java: ['17', '21', '25']
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Whole-stack floor is Java 17 (maven.compiler.release=17; JNA native binding,
      # thread-local environment); the matrix proves every LTS from 17.
      - name: Set up JDK ${{ matrix.java }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java }}
          cache: maven

      # The renderer jar embeds the Rust cdylib (built by the rust job). Restore it
      # into the debug dir the jar-embed step copies.
      - name: Download the Rust renderer dylib
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug

      - name: Test reactor (incl. the SSR web demos)
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -q -B test

  web-client:
    name: Web client (TypeScript DOM renderer)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: lib/typescript/package-lock.json

      - name: Install, typecheck, test, build
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run typecheck
          npm test
          npm run build

      # The demos serve the committed bundle from their static resource dirs
      # (content-hashed dom-renderer-<sha256>.js + the dom-renderer.current
      # pointer; stale hashed copies are pruned); copying the freshly built one
      # must not change the working tree.
      - name: Verify the committed bundle matches the source (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: |
          npm run copy-to-demos
          git diff --exit-code -- lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/src/main/resources lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo/src/main/resources

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, 'docs/**', 'feature/**', 'fix/**', 'spec/**']
  pull_request:

jobs:
  rust:
    name: Rust (workspace + C ABI + no_std/wasm)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # The workspace includes pathland-render-gtk (GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer)
      # and pathland-render-qt (Qt Quick), so the runner needs the GTK4,
      # libadwaita, GStreamer, and Qt system libraries before `cargo test` can
      # link them. GStreamer is required because the GTK renderer plays app-driven
      # media through a direct GStreamer playbin (GTK4's own media backend is
      # compiled out of some builds); the plugins are the runtime set the audio
      # stack uses (playbin, volume/audioconvert, mp3 decode). The Qt libraries
      # are installed in the next step.
      - name: Install GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libgtk-4-dev \
            libadwaita-1-dev \
            libglib2.0-dev \
            libcairo2-dev \
            libpango1.0-dev \
            libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-dev \
            libgraphene-1.0-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev \
            gstreamer1.0-plugins-base \
            gstreamer1.0-plugins-good \
            gstreamer1.0-libav

      - name: Install Qt6 (QML/Quick) system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            qt6-base-dev \
            qt6-declarative-dev \
            qt6-declarative-private-dev \
            qt6-multimedia-dev \
            qml6-module-qtqml \
            qml6-module-qtqml-models \
            qml6-module-qtqml-workerscript \
            qml6-module-qtquick \
            qml6-module-qtquick-layouts \
            qml6-module-qtquick-controls \
            qml6-module-qtquick-templates \
            qml6-module-qtquick-window \
            qml6-module-qtmultimedia
        # The dev headers alone don't ship the QML runtime modules; the Qt
        # renderer's offscreen tests instantiate the QML (QtQml + WorkerScript,
        # Items, stacks/Grid via QtQuick.Layouts, Qt Quick Controls, Multimedia)
        # through QQmlComponent, so the qml6-module-* runtime files are required
        # too. Note the Qt6 package names: `-window` (the Qt5 `-window2` name
        # does not exist), and private headers need qt6-declarative-private-dev.

      - name: Install Rust (stable + wasm32 target)
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown

      - name: Cache cargo
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: lib/rust -> target

      - name: Test workspace
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo test

      - name: Qt renderer headless smoke
        working-directory: lib/rust
        env:
          QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen
          QT_QUICK_BACKEND: software
        run: cargo test -p pathland-render-qt

      # The DOM renderer's constants/token conventions and the cross-renderer SSR
      # golden fixtures are GENERATED from Rust (pathland-ts-codegen /
      # pathland-html-golden). Regenerate them here and fail if the committed
      # files drifted — so a renumbered constant or a changed SSR shape can't land
      # without its TS/fixture counterparts.
      - name: Verify generated TS + golden fixtures are current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen
          cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit
          git diff --exit-code -- \
            lib/typescript/src/constants.ts \
            lib/typescript/src/generated \
            lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr

      - name: Build the C ABI (cdylib, used by the Java JNA ring interop / native hosts)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-core-capi

      - name: no_std / wasm32 direction guard
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: ./check-wasm.sh

      # The Java HTML renderer shim needs the Rust renderer cdylib (the jar embeds
      # it so it travels with the artifact). Build it here and hand it to the java
      # job via an artifact.
      - name: Build the HTML renderer cdylib
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-render-html

      - name: Upload the renderer dylib for the java job
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html.so
          retention-days: 1

  java:
    name: Java (Maven reactor, JDK ${{ matrix.java }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [rust]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        java: ['17', '21', '25']
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Whole-stack floor is Java 17 (maven.compiler.release=17; JNA native binding,
      # thread-local environment); the matrix proves every LTS from 17.
      - name: Set up JDK ${{ matrix.java }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java }}
          cache: maven

      # The renderer jar embeds the Rust cdylib (built by the rust job). Restore it
      # into the debug dir the jar-embed step copies.
      - name: Download the Rust renderer dylib
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug

      - name: Test reactor (incl. the SSR web demos)
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -q -B test

  web-client:
    name: Web client (TypeScript DOM renderer)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: lib/typescript/package-lock.json

      - name: Install, typecheck, test, build
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run typecheck
          npm test
          npm run build

      # The demos serve the committed bundle from their static resource dirs
      # (content-hashed dom-renderer-<sha256>.js + the dom-renderer.current
      # pointer; stale hashed copies are pruned); copying the freshly built one
      # must not change the working tree.
      - name: Verify the committed bundle matches the source (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: |
          npm run copy-to-demos
          git diff --exit-code -- lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/src/main/resources lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo/src/main/resources

      # Real-browser guard for the per-window-id service worker: the browser-variance
      # bugs (WebKit reports an empty clientId on navigations; relative cache keys are
      # rejected) only appear in a real worker engine, never in jsdom/happy-dom.
      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit

      - name: Service worker E2E (Chromium + WebKit)
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: npm run test:e2e

**Menu** (Tier 2): `menu.background`, `menu.foreground`, `menu.border`,
`menu.radius`.

**Label** (Tier 2): `label.foreground`, `label.font.size`.

---

## Color Schemes (Light / Dark)

Base token paths define the **light** design. A `dark.`-prefixed path defines
the **dark** design for the same token.

The renderer derives the **effective color scheme** from its platform's native
light/dark signal by default. An application MAY override it for the whole host
with `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` (`platform` / `light` / `dark`); the renderer
applies the override until the application restores `platform`. The
platform-derived signal itself is never carried by the protocol.

### Rules

1. **Base = light.** `color.primary` is the light value; `dark.color.primary`
   is the dark value.
2. A renderer MUST provide **both** light and dark defaults for every Tier 1
   token (platform-appropriate). Dark mode therefore works even when the
   application only overrides base tokens.
3. The application rolls a full theme by overriding base values and — where the
   dark look must differ — `dark.*` values.
4. The renderer MUST **re-resolve** every token-referencing property when the
   effective scheme changes (including a `SET_COLOR_SCHEME` override), and MAY
   animate the transition.
5. A **`DESIGN_TOKEN` reference** whose path starts with `dark.` is an
   **explicit dark-variant reference**: it resolves the bare path against the
   dark layer regardless of the active scheme. (A `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` override
   still uses the `dark.` prefix to select the dark layer.)
6. The `dark.` prefix is the first scheme prefix; the namespace is open so
   custom schemes could follow. Only `light` (base) and `dark` are
   standardized.

---

## Resolution

```
FUNCTION resolveToken(tokenPath, scheme):
    # Walk most-specific → least-specific, applying the dark layer first.
    layers = []
    if scheme == dark:
        layers += [dark.path, dark.parent(path), …dark.root]   # dark.* layer
    layers += [path, parent(path), …root]                       # base layer

    for candidate in layers:
        if appOverrides.has(candidate):
            return appOverrides[candidate]
    for candidate in layers:
        if rendererDefaults.has(candidate):
            return rendererDefaults[candidate]
    return fallbackValue(path)
```

Example — `color.primary` with the **dark** scheme active and only
`dark.color.primary` overridden:

1. `dark.color.primary` — app override → **used**.
2. (Unreached) `color.primary` app override, `dark.color.primary` renderer
   default, etc.

With the **light** scheme active:

1. `color.primary` — app override, else renderer default, else parent/fallback.
   The `dark.*` layer is skipped entirely.

### Generative token families

A **generative family** is a token rule rather than an independent value. Today
the `space` family is generative: `space.<N>` resolves by resolving `space.base`
(the scheme layer and parent fallback apply there) and multiplying by the
numeric leaf parsed from the path. This lets one override (`space.base`) drive
an arbitrarily fine spacing scale without per-step tokens. Only the `space`
family is generative today; other families could follow.

---

## References in properties

Any property whose value type is `COLOR` / `F32` / `STRING` / `ENUM` MAY instead
carry the **`DESIGN_TOKEN`** value type (`0x08`), with `C` = arenaRef to the
token path. The renderer resolves the reference against the token tables and the
current scheme, and re-resolves when the scheme changes.

- This is how a DSL expresses *semantic intent*: `.foregroundStyle(.primary)`
  or `Color.token("color.primary")` emits a token reference, not a packed color.
- A literal value and a token reference are mutually exclusive on a property.
- Because overrides and the scheme are renderer state, a token-typed property
  requires **no re-emission** when a token changes — the renderer re-resolves.
- If a reference cannot be resolved (no override, no renderer default), the
  property is **left unset** and the renderer's own default styling applies;
  resolution NEVER errors and MUST NOT retain a previously resolved value.
- `META::RESET_THEME` clears every application override (base + `dark.*`) and
  re-resolves all token-referencing properties against the renderer defaults.
  A replacement theme is emitted as `RESET_THEME` followed by its
  `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides in the same frame.

---

## Renderer Responsibilities

A renderer MUST:

1. Provide platform-appropriate **light and dark defaults** for all Tier 1
   tokens.
2. Accept `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` commands and store overrides, and clear
   them on `META::RESET_THEME`.
3. Derive the effective color scheme from the platform (or honor
   `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME`) and re-resolve on change.
4. Resolve token references (`DESIGN_TOKEN` value type) in properties, including
   explicit `dark.` references.
5. Fall back to defaults when no override exists; leave the property unset when
   the reference cannot be resolved.
6. Never transmit visual styling rules in the protocol.

A renderer MAY:

- Map tokens onto native semantic resources (system colors, platform
  typography) for its defaults.
- **Ignore** individual tokens it cannot apply (Tier 2, or Tier 1 tokens
  without a native equivalent) — the "allowed and ignored" rule modifiers use.
- Quantize / approximate token values to platform capabilities (e.g. RGB565
  color depth on embedded displays, limited font sets).

An application MAY override any token via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (base and `dark.*`)
and reference any token in a property; it MUST NOT assume specific default

4. **Property resolution** — any property carrying a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference

**Label** (Tier 2): `label.foreground`, `label.font.size`.

---

## Color Schemes (Light / Dark)

Base token paths define the **light** design. A `dark.`-prefixed path defines
the **dark** design for the same token.

The renderer derives the **effective color scheme** from its platform's native
light/dark signal by default. An application MAY override it for the whole host
with `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` (`platform` / `light` / `dark`); the renderer
applies the override until the application restores `platform`. The
platform-derived signal itself is never carried by the protocol.

### Rules

1. **Base = light.** `color.primary` is the light value; `dark.color.primary`
   is the dark value.
2. A renderer MUST provide **both** light and dark defaults for every Tier 1
   token (platform-appropriate). Dark mode therefore works even when the
   application only overrides base tokens.
3. The application rolls a full theme by overriding base values and — where the
   dark look must differ — `dark.*` values.
4. The renderer MUST **re-resolve** every token-referencing property when the
   effective scheme changes (including a `SET_COLOR_SCHEME` override), and MAY
   animate the transition.
5. A **`DESIGN_TOKEN` reference** whose path starts with `dark.` is an
   **explicit dark-variant reference**: it resolves the bare path against the
   dark layer regardless of the active scheme. (A `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` override
   still uses the `dark.` prefix to select the dark layer.)
6. The `dark.` prefix is the first scheme prefix; the namespace is open so
   custom schemes could follow. Only `light` (base) and `dark` are
   standardized.

---

## Resolution

```
FUNCTION resolveToken(tokenPath, scheme):
    # Walk most-specific → least-specific, applying the dark layer first.
    layers = []
    if scheme == dark:
        layers += [dark.path, dark.parent(path), …dark.root]   # dark.* layer
    layers += [path, parent(path), …root]                       # base layer

    for candidate in layers:
        if appOverrides.has(candidate):
            return appOverrides[candidate]
    for candidate in layers:
        if rendererDefaults.has(candidate):
            return rendererDefaults[candidate]
    return fallbackValue(path)
```

Example — `color.primary` with the **dark** scheme active and only
`dark.color.primary` overridden:

1. `dark.color.primary` — app override → **used**.
2. (Unreached) `color.primary` app override, `dark.color.primary` renderer
   default, etc.

With the **light** scheme active:

1. `color.primary` — app override, else renderer default, else parent/fallback.
   The `dark.*` layer is skipped entirely.

### Generative token families

A **generative family** is a token rule rather than an independent value. Today
the `space` family is generative: `space.<N>` resolves by resolving `space.base`
(the scheme layer and parent fallback apply there) and multiplying by the
numeric leaf parsed from the path. This lets one override (`space.base`) drive
an arbitrarily fine spacing scale without per-step tokens. Only the `space`
family is generative today; other families could follow.

---

## References in properties

Any property whose value type is `COLOR` / `F32` / `STRING` / `ENUM` MAY instead
carry the **`DESIGN_TOKEN`** value type (`0x08`), with `C` = arenaRef to the
token path. The renderer resolves the reference against the token tables and the
current scheme, and re-resolves when the scheme changes.

- This is how a DSL expresses *semantic intent*: `.foregroundStyle(.primary)`
  or `Color.token("color.primary")` emits a token reference, not a packed color.
- A literal value and a token reference are mutually exclusive on a property.
- Because overrides and the scheme are renderer state, a token-typed property
  requires **no re-emission** when a token changes — the renderer re-resolves.
- If a reference cannot be resolved (no override, no renderer default), the
  property is **left unset** and the renderer's own default styling applies;
  resolution NEVER errors and MUST NOT retain a previously resolved value.
- `META::RESET_THEME` clears every application override (base + `dark.*`) and
  re-resolves all token-referencing properties against the renderer defaults.
  A replacement theme is emitted as `RESET_THEME` followed by its
  `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides in the same frame.

A renderer MUST:

1. Provide platform-appropriate **light and dark defaults** for all Tier 1

3. Derive the effective color scheme from the platform (or honor

4. Resolve token references (`DESIGN_TOKEN` value type) in properties, including

5. Fall back to defaults when no override exists; leave the property unset when
   the reference cannot be resolved.
6. Never transmit visual styling rules in the protocol.

A renderer MAY:

- Map tokens onto native semantic resources (system colors, platform

- **Ignore** individual tokens it cannot apply (Tier 2, or Tier 1 tokens

/// The four lookup tables a renderer consults, in resolution order:
/// app overrides (base + `dark.*`) and renderer defaults (base + `dark.*`).
///
/// Overrides and defaults are keyed by **full path** in the base maps and by
/// **bare path** (the `dark.` prefix stripped) in the `dark` maps.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct TokenTables<'a> {
    pub overrides: &'a BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>,
    pub dark_overrides: &'a BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>,
    pub defaults: &'a BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>,
    pub dark_defaults: &'a BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>,
}

///
/// Resolution (spec/TOKENS.md):
/// 1. The **generative `space.<N>` family** resolves `space.base` (scheme-aware,
///    with the same fallback chain) and multiplies by the numeric leaf.
/// 2. Walk the candidate chain — for the dark scheme, `dark.<path>` ancestors
///    first, then the base ancestors; for light, base ancestors only.
/// 3. The first **app override** in the chain wins; otherwise the first
///    **renderer default**; otherwise `None` (the renderer falls back).

    path: &str,
    scheme: Scheme,
    tables: &TokenTables<'_>,
) -> Option<TokenValue> {

/// Convert a single opcode into a human-readable line (debugging aid).
pub fn describe(op: &Opcode) -> String {
    match (op.category(), op.command()) {
        (category::TREE, tree::CREATE_NODE) => {
            format!("TREE:CREATE_NODE id={} type=0x{:04x}", op.a(), op.b() as u16)
        }
        (category::TREE, tree::DELETE_NODE) => format!("TREE:DELETE_NODE id={}", op.a()),
        (category::TREE, tree::INSERT_CHILD) => format!(
            "TREE:INSERT_CHILD parent={} child={} index={}",
            op.a(),
            op.b(),
            op.c()
        ),
        (category::TREE, tree::REMOVE_CHILD) => {
            format!("TREE:REMOVE_CHILD parent={} child={}", op.a(), op.b())
        }
        (category::TREE, tree::MOVE_CHILD) => format!(
            "TREE:MOVE_CHILD parent={} child={} index={}",
            op.a(),
            op.b(),
            op.c()

/// The packed wire value (`C` field) for non-string values. `Str` returns
    /// `None` — the wire carries an arena ref there.
    pub fn to_bits(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        match self {
            TokenValue::Color(v) => Some(*v),
            TokenValue::F32(v) => Some(v.to_bits()),
            TokenValue::U32(v) => Some(*v),
            TokenValue::U8(v) => Some(u32::from(*v)),
            TokenValue::I32(v) => Some(*v as u32),
            TokenValue::Str(_) => None,
        }
    }
}

The grep over generated JS is noisy. The TS generated token conventions are embedded in the built bundle but that's fine. No TS source hardcodes `--pl-color-text-on-primary`. The TS CSS uses var from path overrides. So fixing built-in to canonical onPrimary is better.

But note: if an app previously sent `color.text.onPrimary`, with our fixed CSS it will now work. Good.

Now, check `lib/typescript/src/tokens.ts` maybe tests assert built-in CSS tokens? The DOM client doesn't use built-in CSS. Fine.

Now, the Java HTML renderer tests might compare SSR output and include CSS? The JNA render returns full document; tests may check contains. Let's grep Java tests for `--pl-` etc (excluding built resources). Use include filters.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Sync the generated HTML base design into the Rust renderer crate.
#
# The canonical source lives in design/ (Style Dictionary tokens + hand-authored
# reset/components CSS). `design/build/base.css` is the generated bundle the
# renderer embeds with `include_str!`. Run `npm --prefix design run build` first.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/sync-design-css.sh           copy the bundle into the crate
#   scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check   fail if the committed crate copy drifted
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
SRC="$ROOT/design/build/base.css"
DEST_DIR="$ROOT/lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets"
DEST="$DEST_DIR/base.css"

check=0
if [[ "${1:-}" == "--check" ]]; then
  check=1
elif [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
  echo "usage: $0 [--check]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

if [[ ! -f "$SRC" ]]; then
  echo "sync-design-css: missing $SRC — run 'npm --prefix design run build' first" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ $check -eq 1 ]]; then
  if [[ ! -f "$DEST" ]]; then
    echo "sync-design-css: missing $DEST — run scripts/sync-design-css.sh" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  if ! diff -u "$DEST" "$SRC"; then
    echo "sync-design-css: crate CSS is stale — run 'npm --prefix design run build && scripts/sync-design-css.sh'" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "sync-design-css: up to date"
  exit 0
fi

mkdir -p "$DEST_DIR"
cp "$SRC" "$DEST"
echo "sync-design-css: wrote $DEST"

input.content:
# Pathland base design

The built-in look of the HTML renderer, generated from a **three-layer Style
Dictionary pipeline** plus hand-authored reset/component CSS.

```
tokens/base/*.tokens.json        internal palette + scales          (not emitted)
tokens/semantic/*.tokens.json    protocol catalog semantics        (emitted)
tokens/component/*.tokens.json   per-component surface             (emitted)
html/reset.css                   Tailwind-derived preflight        (hand-authored)
html/components.css              .pathland-* rules                 (hand-authored)
```

The generated bundle is `build/base.css` (reset + `tokens.css` + components).
`lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/base.css` is the synced, committed
copy the renderer embeds with `include_str!`; the renderer has one built-in base
design and no app-facing design selection.

## Commands

```sh
npm --prefix design ci          # install (CI / clean checkout)
npm --prefix design run build   # Style Dictionary + build/base.css
npm --prefix design run check   # catalog/layer/dark/dimension validation
npm --prefix design run dev     # rebuild on token/CSS changes
npm --prefix design run dev -- --serve   # also serve preview/ on :4173
scripts/sync-design-css.sh      # copy build/base.css into the Rust crate
scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check
```

After changing tokens or CSS: `npm --prefix design run build`, then
`scripts/sync-design-css.sh`, then run `cargo test -p pathland-render-html`.

`build/` and `node_modules/` are gitignored. `package-lock.json` is committed.

## Tokens

Each token is a flat DTCG entry: `$value`, `$type`, optional `$description` and
`$extensions.pathland`. Keys carry their full dotted path because the catalog
contains paths that are both a leaf and a group (`control.border` is a color,
`control.border.width` is a dimension), which nested DTCG trees cannot represent.

- **base** tokens are literals. They are internal: the generator resolves them
  to literals and **never emits them** as CSS variables. Override the semantic
  or component token instead.
- **semantic** tokens reference base tokens. They are the protocol catalog
  surface (`spec/TOKENS.md`).
- **component** tokens reference semantic tokens, or a base scale token
  (`base.space.*`, `base.radius.*`, `base.border.width.*`, `base.size.*`,
  `base.font.*`) when no semantic alias exists. A component token that must
  reference a base **color** needs an explicit justification:

  ```json
  "$extensions": {
    "pathland": { "baseReference": "why this base color is used directly" }
  }
  ```

### Dark values

Dark values live on `$extensions.pathland.dark`:

```json
{
  "color.primary": {
    "$value": "{base.color.blue.600}",
    "$type": "color",
    "$extensions": { "pathland": { "dark": "{base.color.blue.400}" } }
  }
}
```

The generator emits four token layers:

1. `:root` (light),
2. `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) :root:not([data-pathland-scheme])`,
3. `:root[data-pathland-scheme='dark']` (forced dark) and
   `:root[data-pathland-scheme='light']` (forced light),
4. the forced-dark variable family `--pl-dark-*` for explicit `dark.` token
   references.

A reference to another **emitted** token compiles to `var(--pl-<target>)` (and
`var(--pl-dark-<target>)` in the forced-dark family), so the target's dark layer
wins. A reference to a **base** token compiles to its literal. With no explicit
dark value, the dark layers reference the same target variable.

### Internal tokens

Durations, z-index, and `em` icon sizes are renderer-internal (not part of
`spec/TOKENS.md`). Mark them with `$extensions.pathland.internal: true`; they are
still emitted and listed in `build/manifest.json` with `"internal": true`.

## Validation

`npm run check` enforces:

- every Tier-1 token in `pathland_core::TIER1_TOKENS` is present;
- layer direction (semantic → base, component → semantic/base scale) and
  no unresolved references;
- every emitted token has light, platform-dark, forced-dark-scheme, and
  forced-dark variable declarations;
- every `$type: dimension` token is recognized by the canonical
  `isLengthToken` rules in `pathland-render-html::token_spec` (add a rule there
  when introducing a new dimension path);
- durations / z-index / icon sizes are marked internal;
- `build/manifest.json` and `build/tokens.css` match the current sources, and
  base tokens are not emitted.

## Preview

`preview/index.html` loads `build/base.css` and renders representative
`.pathland-*` markup (buttons, fields, toggles, slider, progress, stepper, menu,
media) with a light/dark/system switcher. Run `npm run dev -- --serve` and open
<http://127.0.0.1:4173/>. This is a development tool, not an app-selectable base
design.

## Generated files — do not edit

- `build/tokens.css`
- `build/manifest.json`
- `build/base.css`
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/base.css` (synced copy)

Edit the token files or `html/{reset,components}.css`, then rebuild and sync.

    <description>
        The Java binding to the Rust HTML renderer (dev.pathland.render.html): a
        thin JNA shim over libpathland_render_html (pathland_html_render /
        _render_fragment / _free). Stateless: each call renders
        a full snapshot frame to HTML in one pass. The server-side/remote-projection
        target, usable from Spring Boot, Quarkus, or any Java server. The single
        renderer is the Rust crate reused by every language.
    </description>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-view</artifactId>

        <dependency>

            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <configuration>
                    <!-- Point the test JVM at the Rust renderer cdylib; absent the

                    <argLine>-Djava.library.path=${project.basedir}/../../rust/target/debug</argLine>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>

            <!-- Embed the Rust renderer dylib in the jar so it travels with the
                 artifact (JNA extracts it at runtime — no java.library.path needed).
                 Copies the host-platform build into META-INF/native/. Fails loudly
                 when the dylib is missing (the CI rust job builds it; locally run
                 cargo build first). -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-antrun-plugin</artifactId>
                <executions>

                        <id>embed-native-renderer</id>
                        <phase>process-resources</phase>

                                    <os family="mac" />
                                </condition>
                                <condition property="pathland.native.ext" value=".dll">

                                </condition>
                                <condition property="pathland.native.ext" value=".so">

                                </condition>
                                <property name="pathland.native.ext" value="" />

                                     this copies each into META-INF/native/<os>-<arch>/.
                                     A local build has no staging dir and instead
                                     embeds the host Rust debug build in the flat
                                     META-INF/native/ layout. -->
                                <property name="pathland.native.staging" value="${project.basedir}/target/native" />
                                <available file="${pathland.native.staging}" type="dir" property="pathland.native.staged" />
                                <property name="pathland.native.host" value="${project.basedir}/../../rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html${pathland.native.ext}" />

                                    <condition>
                                        <and>

                                            <not><isset property="pathland.native.host.present" /></not>
                                        </and>
                                    </condition>

                                <!-- Release: copy each staged platform dir verbatim. -->
                                <copy todir="${project.build.outputDirectory}/META-INF/native">
                                    <fileset dir="${pathland.native.staging}" includes="*/*" erroronmissingdir="false" />
                                </copy>
                                <!-- Local dev: embed the host lib in the flat layout. -->
                                <copy file="${pathland.native.host}"
                                      tofile="${project.build.outputDirectory}/META-INF/native/libpathland_render_html${pathland.native.ext}"
                                      failonerror="false" />
                            </target>
                        </configuration>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>run</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

We have enough. Notice `scripts/run-quarkus-demo.sh` and `run-spring-demo.sh` call `build_rust_html`, which now runs design build + sync, then cargo build. Then `java_install` (mvn install) installs the Java artifacts including the `pathland-render-html` jar with the freshly built dylib embedded. Then runs quarkus:dev or packages spring jar. So for Java demos, the simplest answer is: just rerun the demo script; `build_rust_html` now does the design build + sync automatically. But note `java_install` skips the two web demos and installs `pathland-render-html`, which embeds the dylib. So run script is enough.

For a running Quarkus dev mode: changes to the Rust dylib embedded in the installed jar might not be picked up without restart. `mvn quarkus:dev` could hot-reload Java classes but the native lib is extracted from the jar at startup; the jar is newly installed by java_install before starting. Since the script rebuilds and then starts, fine. If already running, stop and rerun script.

For the HTML preview (design changes only, no server): `npm --prefix design run dev -- --serve` gives instant preview. Or `npm --prefix design run dev` rebuilds base.css while you browse preview/index.html (refresh).

For the Rust GTK/Qt demos: They do not use the HTML base design; token changes won't show. If you want to see tokens in a native renderer, those renderers use their own defaults (render-core host defaults in Rust), not design/tokens. So the design token change only affects HTML/SSR/DOM clients.

Could mention the one-liner:
```
npm --prefix design run build && scripts/sync-design-css.sh
```
then for HTML demos:
- Quarkus: `scripts/run-quarkus-demo.sh`
- Spring: `scripts/run-spring-demo.sh`
- Fastest visual check: `npm --prefix design run dev -- --serve` (preview) or rerun `cargo run -p pathland-render-html`? There isn't an HTML demo crate other than the web demos.

But if they want the demo app already running in Quarkus dev mode, the script's `build_rust_html` + `java_install` run before starting. If already running, restart.

Need also mention maybe `npm --prefix design run check` to validate tokens. And `scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check` as a sanity check.

Also, important nuance: For Spring/Quarkus, running `mvn quarkus:dev` directly (without script) will use the installed `pathland-render-html` jar from `~/.m2`, which may have a stale embedded dylib. So either rerun the script (which does `mvn install`) or run `mvn -P refresh-ide validate` then `mvn install`? The script is best. The AGENTS says for Spring prefer fat jar. So advise script.

For Quarkus dev mode, `java_install` installs updated jars to local repo. Then `quarkus:dev` uses them. Good.

Could also mention if they're iterating on tokens only and using the browser demo, they can run `npm --prefix design run dev -- --serve` to see the design preview without rebuilding Rust; but the actual demo needs the Rust rebuild.

parts.text:
We have enough to answer. The question: "Am I missing something. Should the css not be served as a separate cacheable file?"

Answer: No, not missing a bug; the plan explicitly deferred a production hashed linked stylesheet, and the renderer currently inlines the base CSS. Explain tradeoffs. If they want it now, propose a plan. Since plan mode, we should present a plan and ask whether to implement. Need possibly explore more details for a robust plan: how to compute a hash, how to expose CSS via C ABI/Java shim, route serving, SSR link vs inline, token overrides still inline, first-paint FOUC considerations, no-JS, demo support, tests, cache headers. Let's think.

Current architecture:
- Rust `render_document` emits `<style>` built-in CSS + optional `<style data-pathland-tokens>` overrides + fit styles.
- The full CSS is embedded in every SSR HTML response (dylib/C ABI).
- The Java starters serve `/_pathland/**` from classpath/static or icons from Rust.
- The TypeScript DOM client hydrates, and token overrides are managed via a `<style data-pathland-tokens>` element.
- The plan (design/PLAN.md) includes under Non-goals: "A production hashed linked stylesheet (deferred; the renderer embeds the base CSS)." And Deferred: "Production hashed linked stylesheet for the single built-in design."
- The AGENTS "HTML base design" section says renderer embeds the base CSS.

So user is likely noticing that inline CSS is not cacheable and asking if it should be separate. The correct response: It's a deliberate deferred tradeoff, not an oversight. But we can offer to implement it.

We need discuss:
- Pros of separate CSS: cacheable/immutable, smaller SSR payload, no repeated style parsing per page/navigation, easier CDN, browser can cache across sessions. With inline, each SSR response repeats ~20KB; gzip/brotli reduces but still per-navigation and no cross-page cache? Actually inline CSS in each HTML is compressed with HTML and prevents long-term caching; on every full navigation the browser re-downloads and reparses. On SPA/WS deltas, navigation is client-side so CSS stays, but SSR first paint and reloads repeat.
- Cons/costs: an extra request (unless preloaded), FOUC/FOIT if CSS not loaded before paint, base design is single and small, offline no-JS still works but extra request; SSR must know the hashed URL; hosts must serve it; token overrides remain inline; tests/goldens change; caching semantics and version skew between server/dylib and asset. Inline is robust and simple for the POC; clients get CSS with the HTML (no race). Also the CSS is generated and embedded in the dylib jar, so serving from the Rust host avoids static file duplication.
- The plan deliberately deferred this. So answer: "No, you're not missing something in the implementation; it's an explicit deferred non-goal."

Then propose implementation plan if wanted:
1. Generate a content hash for `base.css` in the design build (e.g., `manifest.json` includes `hash`, or Rust computes at compile time). Since Rust embeds it, we can expose the CSS and a hash via the C ABI (e.g., `pathland_html_base_css()` + `pathland_html_base_css_name()` or a single `builtin_css`/`builtin_css_hash`). Better: compute hash at design build and embed `base.css` plus `base-css.current` name? But the Rust crate should not depend on Node at runtime. The build can write a small `assets/base.css.hash` or generate a Rust file. Or compute hash at compile time with a build script. A build.rs could hash `assets/base.css` using a simple hash (or use `std::hash`? need stable). Simpler: design build writes `design/build/manifest.json` with a hash and sync writes `assets/base.css` plus a generated `assets/base.css.name` (e.g. `base-<sha256-12>.css`). But extra file. Alternatively, Rust `include_str!` and compute FNV-1a at startup/once via `OnceLock`, exposing `builtin_css_hash`/`builtin_css_url`. Content hash doesn't need cryptographic strength; but cache busting benefits from stable, collision-resistant. FNV okay for POC; SHA-256 would require dependency or build script. We could have design build compute SHA-256 and write `design/build/base.css.hash` or include in manifest; sync copies a generated `assets/base.css.name`. But then Rust needs that string; `include_str!` on a name file. Or generate a tiny `assets/base.css.name` file. Hmm.
2. Renderer API: add a mode/flag to `HtmlRenderer` (e.g., `with_external_css(true)` or `render_document_with_css`) that emits `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/_pathland/base-<hash>.css">` instead of `<style>`. Keep default inline for backward compat/tests. Also `render_document` could detect host-provided base URL. Add a C ABI function to get the base CSS and its URL/name: `pathland_html_base_css()` and `pathland_html_base_css_name()`/`..._url()`. Java shim exposes `HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` / `baseCssName()`.
3. Host routing:
   - Spring `PathlandIndexController.framework`: if file matches `base-<hash>.css`, serve bytes from `HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, `Content-Type: text/css`, maybe ETag. Same for Quarkus `IndexResource.frameworkFile` (both global and per-app).
   - Ensure no static file dependency. This mirrors icons served from Rust.
   - Maybe also support global and per-app base path: SSR link should use `/_pathland/base-<hash>.css` or `{data-pathland-base}/base-...`? The page emits `data-pathland-base` perhaps. Need inspect how index HTML is formed: `PathlandIndexController.index` returns raw html; DOM client reads `document.documentElement.dataset.pathlandBase ?? "/_pathland"`. For mounted apps, SSR link should resolve to the same base. Does the renderer know `data-pathland-base`? Let's search. There is likely a meta or data attribute on html from the server/session.  # Pathland Project - AI Agent Guide
 
 This document provides essential context for AI agents (or human contributors) working on the **Pathland** protocol. It captures the project's direction, architectural decisions, and implementation details to ensure consistency.
 
 **Last Updated**: October 28, 2026
 
 ---
 
 ## Architecture: Rust Opcode Engine
 
 > The canonical core is a **Rust engine** that emits the application's
 > **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding,
 > alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared linear
 > memory, consumed by host renderers. View components and modifiers are written
 > in Rust with a SwiftUI-like API, and in Java with the hand-written
 > **`com.pathland.view` DSL** (reusable library, Java 17+); both drive the engine
 > through the flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a zero-copy shared
 > ring on desktop.
 
 ### The 16-byte Opcode Engine
 
 - Every opcode is exactly **16 bytes**: `Category (1B) | Command ID (1B) | Flags (2B) | A (4B) | B (4B) | C (4B)`, `#[repr(C, packed)]`, little-endian.
 - A 64-byte cache line holds exactly **4 opcodes** → L1-cache-friendly.
 - Opcodes live in a **ring buffer** in linear memory; the guest writes at `writeCursor`, the host reads from `readCursor`; frame boundaries via a monotonic `frameCount` in the header block.
 - **Both directions are binary**: a second **event ring** (host → guest) carries `EVENT`-category opcodes. The renderer writes raw inputs at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains them at `eventReadCursor`. Events are 16-byte opcodes through the engine, never a side-channel callback.
 - **Variable-length data** (strings, token paths) lives in a bump **arena**; opcodes reference entries by offset (`[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`), so every opcode stays 16 bytes. A second host-owned **event arena** mirrors this in the host → guest direction (shared-memory event strings, e.g. `TEXT_CHANGED`); over the network, host → guest strings ride the batch's string section.
 - Spec: **`spec/OPCODE.md`** (primary) + **`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`** (golden vectors). Companion catalogs: **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`** (views), **`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** (modifiers/properties), **`spec/EVENTS.md`** (events), **`spec/LAYOUT.md`** (frame & layout allocation contract) — draft IDs are allocated there spec-first.
 
 ### Declarative, not positioned (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The engine describes WHAT the UI is — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
 > padding, alignment — never WHERE it is. It does not compute layout and does
 > not emit rects.**
 
 - The engine emits **declarative structure** (`TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move) + **constraint properties** (`PARAMETER` spacing/padding/alignment/FILL/HUG hints).
 - **Native elements everywhere**: each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that platform's native elements — GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the browser, HTML server-side — and those native elements lay themselves out. Never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent.
 - **Reactive emission**: emission is diff-based. Only the nodes that changed emit opcodes (property diffs via `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`, structural diffs via `TREE` opcodes). An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes. Signals in the application mark the tree dirty; the engine reconciles.
 - **Zero dynamic heap allocations** during steady-state emission (proven by test).
 
 ### no_std / wasm32 direction guard (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 `pathland-core` and `pathland-view` must remain `#![no_std]` + `alloc` and
 compile for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. This is the guarantee that the protocol
 core can still target a browser / embedded / remote projection later (goal #15,
 Quarkus SSR + WebSocket). The desktop path (`pathland-view-native`) is the only
 consumer today, but the core must not become desktop-only. Verify with
 `lib/rust/check-wasm.sh` (i.e. `cargo build -p pathland-core -p pathland-view
 --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`).
 
 ### Reactive signals (Angular-style)
 
 `pathland-core::signal` provides writable signals that live in the engine. A
 node binds its text (`Node::text_binding`), a property
 (`Node::property_bindings`) or a **string property** (`Node::string_bindings`,
 e.g. a media controller's `MEDIA_SOURCE`) to a `SignalId`; during emit the engine
 resolves the binding and records the dependency, and `Engine::set_signal`
 re-emits **only the bound nodes** (`SET_TEXT` / `SET_PROPERTY`) — no full tree
 walk. Signal values
 are one of `F32`/`U32`/`Bool`/`Enum`/`Str` (packed to the wire's `u32` value or
 arena string). Foreign hosts reach signals via the flat C ABI
 (`pathland_native_signal_create_*` / `signal_set_*` / `node_bind_text` /
 `node_bind_property`) and the Java `Signal` type. Binding then calling `emit`
 records the dependency; a subsequent `set` is a partial emit. (Computed/derived
 signals + effects are the planned next step.)
 
 ### Rust Workspace (`lib/rust/`)
 
 ```
 # ── The three elements ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 crates/pathland-view/     # RETAINED UI — SwiftUI-style view DSL: VStack/HStack/Text/Button +
                           #   decoupled modifiers (spacing/padding/fontSize/color/background)
                           #   + Video (a MediaController's surface) + attach() (no_std)
 crates/pathland-core/     # PROTOCOL — 16-byte opcode, ring buffer, arena, constants, events,
                           #   memory layout, Guest/Host/Frame surface (no_std, zero-alloc).
                           #   Pure protocol; the emitter moved out to pathland-engine.
 crates/pathland-engine/   # EMITTER — retained tree types (Node/Component) + the diff-based
                           #   reactive emitter + signals + MediaController (spec/MEDIA.md).
 crates/pathland-core-transport/ # TRANSPORT — shared-memory ring owner (RingTransport) +
                           #   network batch encode/decode + batching policy (std)
 crates/pathland-render-core/ # RENDERER CORE (shared, toolkit-free) — opcode-frame decode into a
                           #   native-element description (RenderTree/HostNode), design-token
                           #   tables + resolution, concrete Tier-1 defaults. No GTK/Qt: every
                           #   renderer shares one tested decode path.
 crates/pathland-render-gtk/ # RENDERER — maps opcode frames onto native GTK widgets
                           #   incrementally; the only crate that touches GTK/glib/pango.
                           #   Fixed-size images scale to the logical-points box (gdk-pixbuf,
                           #   CONTENT_MODE fit/fill). App-driven media via a direct GStreamer
                           #   playbin (GTK4's own media backend is compiled out of some
                           #   builds). Exposes pathland_gtk_run[_ring]/
 ```

 ### HTML base design (`design/`)
 
 The HTML renderer's built-in stylesheet is generated from a **three-layer Style
 Dictionary pipeline** plus hand-authored reset/component CSS (one built-in base
 design; no app-facing base-design selection):
 
 ```
 design/tokens/base/*.tokens.json      # internal palette + scales (not emitted)
 design/tokens/semantic/*.tokens.json  # protocol catalog semantics (emitted)
 design/tokens/component/*.tokens.json # per-component surface (emitted)
 design/html/{reset,components}.css    # hand-authored CSS consuming var(--pl-*)
 design/scripts/{build,dev,check}.mjs  # SD build, watcher/preview, validation
 design/build/base.css                 # generated: reset + tokens + components
+design/build/base.css.name            # content hash: base-<sha256-12>.css
 ```
 
 - Tokens are flat DTCG entries (`$value`/`$type`/`$extensions.pathland`) because
   the catalog has both leaf and group paths (`control.border` vs
   `control.border.width`). Dark values live on `$extensions.pathland.dark`;
   durations/z-index/`em` icon sizes are marked internal.
-- `npm --prefix design run build` generates `design/build/{tokens.css,manifest.json,base.css}`;
+- `npm --prefix design run build` generates
+  `design/build/{tokens.css,manifest.json,base.css,base.css.name}`;
   `npm --prefix design run check` validates catalog coverage, layer direction,
-  dark/forced-dark declarations, and dimension/`isLengthToken` rules.
-- `scripts/sync-design-css.sh` copies the bundle to
-  `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/base.css` (committed; `--check`
-  fails on drift). `css.rs` embeds it with `include_str!`.
+  dark/forced-dark declarations, dimension/`isLengthToken` rules, and the CSS
+  content hash.
+- `scripts/sync-design-css.sh` copies the bundle + name to
+  `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/` (committed; `--check` fails on
+  drift). `css.rs` embeds both with `include_str!` (`builtin_css()` /
+  `builtin_css_name()`).
+- The renderer's library default is inline (`render_document`); the linked mode
+  (`render_document_linked`, C ABI `pathland_html_render_linked` +
+  `pathland_html_base_css[_name]`, Java `renderLinked`/`baseCss`/`baseCssName`)
+  emits `{base}/base-<hash>.css`. The Spring Boot and Quarkus starters use it
+  and serve the renderer-owned bytes immutable (global + mounted bases); token
+  overrides/fit rules stay inline.
 - `scripts/lib.sh` (`build_rust_html`), the Maven `refresh-ide` profile, and CI
   run the design build + sync. Do not edit generated CSS by hand.
 
 ### Native C-ABI shim (`pathland-view-native` + `pathland-core-capi`)
 
 The **desktop/cross-language zero-copy path**: `pathland-view-native` exposes the
 flat world (the flat `builder`/`engine` surface) as `pathland_native_*` C
 functions with a **shared-memory ring** the host driver reads in place. Any
 language that links the dylib (Swift/Java/C# via FFI) calls the flat surface —
 no per-component wrappers — and consumes opcodes zero-copy.
 
 `pathland-core-capi` (`libpathland_core`) is the **minimal ring C ABI** for the
 Java DSL: `pathland_core_create`/`destroy`, `pathland_ring_buffer_push` (one
 raw 16-byte opcode), `pathland_core_arena_alloc`, frame boundaries, zero-copy
 `ring_ptr`/`ring_len`, and event drain/send. The Java DSL
 (`com.pathland.view.ffm`) binds it with **JNA** (lazily loaded, zero JNI) and
 owns the retained tree + diff emission itself.
 
 ### GTK4 Renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`)
 
 The desktop renderer: a single crate that owns **all** GTK/glib/pango usage and
 maps opcode frames **incrementally** onto native GTK widgets (a retained
 `id → gtk::Widget` map). Both the Rust demo and the Java demo render through
 it — the demos **never call GTK or Swing directly**:
 
 - Rust demo links `pathland-render-gtk` as an `rlib` and calls `GtkRenderer::run(...)`
   with a wake closure.
 - Java demo (`pathland-gtk-demo`) loads `pathland-render-gtk` as a `cdylib` via JNA and
   calls `pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` over the Java DSL's own
   `libpathland_core` ring; native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes through the shared
   ring. The renderer **writes** the events and **wakes** the host (no payload); the host
   drains the event ring itself via `pathland_core_drain_events`. Events are never
   delivered through a side-channel callback — they flow through the opcode engine.
   The demo mounts `MusicPlayerView` (the same shared views the web demos use) with the
   app-driven media contract: the renderer plays the tracks through a direct GStreamer
   `playbin` and reports `MEDIA_*` events back; the demo's web-style
   `/_pathland/assets/...` paths resolve against an extracted local asset root
   (`pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`).
 
 The renderer maps native inputs onto the raw `Event` surface via GTK4
 controllers (`Button::clicked` → pointer up, `EventControllerMotion` →
 pointer move/enter/leave), emitting events through the same `Pump::send_input`
 path.
 
 `pathland_gtk::run` passes an explicit empty argv to GTK (the process command
 line belongs to the embedding host — e.g. the JVM's `-cp`/`-D` flags — and must
 not be parsed as GTK options).
 
 ### Native Java DSL (`com.pathland.view`, in `lib/java/pathland-view`)
 
 The **hand-written, zero-dependency Java 17+ DSL** (no codegen). It is the
 SwiftUI-like authoring surface shared by desktop, Spring Boot, and Quarkus
 apps. Components and modifiers:
 
 - `View` is an **open interface** — the library ships `Text`/`Image`/`Color`/
   `Rectangle`, `VStack`/`HStack`/`ZStack`, `Spacer`, `Button`,
   `TextField(placeholder, WritableSignal<String>)`, `Video` (a
   `MediaController`'s surface), and application code (Quarkus/Spring/desktop)
   defines its own views by implementing `View`. **Media is a state object, not a
   view** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MediaController` owns the resource + transport as
   signals, a `Video` surface renders it, and **audio has no view** — the app
   binds its own buttons/sliders (`controller.attach()` materializes the
   controller's node once, outside any swapping branch, so a band swap never
   restarts playback).
 - **Custom views and styles use the configurator** (spec DSL.md §2): an
   app-authored `View` with values implements `Configurable<View.Config>`, holds a
   **`private` constructor**, and exposes
   `static ViewBuilder<View, Config> make(Consumer<Config>)`; a style
   (`ButtonStyle`/`LabelStyle`/`VideoStyle`) expose a
   **lowercase static factory** on their own type returning the style value
   (`BorderedButtonStyle.borderedButtonStyle(s -> s…)`), mirroring the library's
   `Modifiers.*` lowercase functions (e.g.
   `borderedButtonStyle(b -> b.padding(..).background(..)…)`). Creation goes
   through the configurator, never a parameterized constructor. The
   `pathland-view-processor` `ViewAuthoringProcessor` **errors** on
   public/protected constructors **with parameters** in custom `View` **and**
   `Style` implementations (no-arg roots and abstract types are exempt), so the
   convention is compile-enforced where the processor is wired
   (`annotationProcessorPaths`). The library's own views/styles follow the same
   shape (`Video`, `Text`, `BorderedButtonStyle`, …).
 - **SwiftUI-style `body()`**: composite views declare `View body()` (their subtree);
   the library's primitives override `render(Environment)` to materialize a
   `PathlandNode`. `body()` is evaluated **once at mount** — reactive values come from
   signals (`Text.make(t -> t.text(Signal))`, `Signals.computed`), not from body
   re-evaluation, so the emitter keeps its fine-grained `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY` deltas.
 - **The three operations (spec DSL.md §2)**: every concrete view exposes
   `make(...)` (values — the only static; `make(Consumer<Config>)`, `make(value)`,
   `make()`), and the instance operations `.modifiers(ViewModifier...)` and
   `.children(View...)` chain on the returned builder. Java's static-vs-instance
   rule means the statics sit on the view class, the chain on the builder; a bare
   `View` value applies modifiers through the interface default
   `View.modifiers(...)`. Values are a
   fluent per-view `Config` (`VStack.make(v -> v.alignment(...).spacing(8))`,
   `Text.make(t -> t.text("hi"))`); modifiers are `ViewModifier` values built by
   the **`Modifiers` facade's lowercase functions** — one
   `import static com.pathland.view.Modifiers.*;` brings the whole modifier
   vocabulary (`padding(p -> p.uniform(16))`, `frame(f -> f.width(100))`,
   `borderedButtonStyle(b -> …)`) — or, for single values, the value itself
   (`FontWeight.BOLD`, `Font.headline()`, a `ButtonStyle`). The `View` interface has
   **no per-modifier sugar** (`font`/`navigate`/`environment`/`onPathChange` were
   removed — use `.modifiers(Font…)`, `.modifiers(NavigationIntent.navigate(…))`,
   `.modifiers(environmentBinding(e -> e.key(…).value(…)))`,
   `.modifiers(pathChange(p -> p.listener(…)))`), and the `*Mod` shims
   (`EnvironmentMod`→`EnvironmentBinding`, `router/NavigationMod`→`NavigationIntent`,
   `PathChangeMod`→`PathChange`, `FontWeightMod`→`FontWeight`, …) are **removed**.
 - **Single-value shortcuts (spec DSL.md §2)**: a view/modifier whose config has a
   designated primary member also exposes a single-value construction overload that
   is pure sugar for the lambda — views construct with `make(value)` / `make(Signal<T>)`
   (`Text.make("hi")`), modifiers with the lowercase function's value form
   (`padding(16)`, `fontSize(sizeSignal)`). Multi-member configs (`Padding.edges`, `Offset`,
   `Gauge`, `Border`, …) have **no** shortcut — use the lambda. The shortcut delegates
   to the same `make(Consumer<Config>)` (views) / `Modifiers` facade
   (modifiers) factory via the package-private
   `Configurators` helper (one construction path). The former `.of(...)` construction
   factories are **removed** — a shortcut (or the lambda / `.children(...)` / empty
   `make()` for config-less views) replaces every one. Only data/branch factories keep
   `of`: `Color.of/rgb/argb/token`, `Case.of`, `Fit.of`, `EnvironmentKey.of`,
   `Route.of`, `Params.of`, `Signals.*`.
   Sizing is the `Frame` modifier value
   (`frame(f -> f.width(w).height(h).alignment(..))` and the lambda
   configurator `frame(f -> f.minWidth(..).maxWidth(..).alignment(..))`
   (min/ideal/max bounds)); all
   compile to the same `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT`/min-max `SET_PROPERTY`s.
   Typed enums
   (`Alignment`/`TextAlignment`/`FontWeight`/`Truncation`), not raw ints.
 - **Environment scoping via a `ThreadLocal`** (Java 17+): a `ButtonStyle` modifier
   injects a style down the whole child tree; `ButtonStyle.makeBody(Configuration)`
   with built-in `PlainButtonStyle` / `BorderedButtonStyle`. Custom wrappers via
   `ViewModifier.body(View)`. The `Environment` also carries the session's
   `PersistentState`.
 - **Reactivity (Angular parity)** in `com.pathland.view.signal`:
   `Signals.signal/computed/effect/untracked` — lazy+memoized computeds,
   glitch-free synchronous flush, equality suppression, error caching, write
   discipline (`allowWrites()`), circular-dependency detection.
 - **Persisted view state** (`com.pathland.view.state`): a `State<T>` field (e.g.
   `State<Integer> count = new State<>(0);`) is auto-wired to the session's
   `PersistentState` (keyed by field name, or `new State<>(0, "key")` for an explicit
   key) by the `pathland-view-processor` annotation processor, which detects `State`
   fields by type and generates a `<View>_StateBinder` per view class. Each view
   connects its own `State` when it renders (`View.render` calls `Environment.state()
   → PersistentState.connect(view)`), so nested views can be instantiated inline in
   `body()` and need not be declared as fields. `PersistentState.signal(name, initial)`
   auto-loads the persisted value and auto-saves on change (key `name:scope`), and
   `StateStore` is untyped (one store serves all signal types).
 - **Fine-grained emitter** (`com.pathland.view.emit`): mounts a view tree once,
   assigns stable ids, and registers a **node-level binding effect** per reactive
   text/property — a signal change re-emits only that node's `SET_TEXT` /
   `SET_PROPERTY` (unchanged signals emit zero opcodes). Sinks: `FrameOpcodeSink`
   (self-contained frames for SSR/WebSocket) and `RingOpcodeSink` (JNA into
   `libpathland_core`). The wire codec (`com.pathland.view.transport`) mirrors
   `pathland_core_transport` (`PLPL` batch format, self-contained frames + events).
 
 Consistency with `pathland_core::constants` is enforced by the emitter/HTML
 tests (golden byte layout + round-trips), replacing the old codegen assert pass.
 
 - **Single signal value convention**: a view or modifier holds **one `Signal<T>`
   field** for a reactive value — never a raw field *plus* a signal field for the
   same value. Static values are authored through the raw config setter (or the
   `.of(T)` convenience), which
   wraps them in `Signals.constant(...)` (e.g. `Text.make(t -> t.text("Hello"))` ≡
   `Text.make(t -> t.text(Signals.constant("Hello")))`); the emitter treats a
   `ConstantSignal` as
   a plain, non-reactive property (no binding/effect), so statics carry zero
   binding overhead. Controls' config fields for *distinct* properties
   (`min`/`max`/`step`/`placeholder`/`mode`/`style`) stay raw.

 ## Project Vision
 
 **Pathland is a cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol** that enables retained-mode UI development with multiple renderer backends. It is **protocol-first**, meaning the protocol specification is the source of truth, not any particular implementation.
 
 **Primary Goal**: Write once, run anywhere - Enable UI code to be written once and deployed across web, mobile, desktop, and embedded platforms through different renderer implementations.
 
 **Status**: The Rust opcode engine (16-byte opcode, ring buffer, arena, diff-based reactive emission) is implemented and tested (`cargo test`). See the Architecture section above.
 
 ---
 
 ## CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES
 
 ### Principle 1: Renderer Statelessness (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The renderer MUST NOT retain application state.**
 
 - Renderers are **pure functions** of the opcode stream: same opcodes → same output
 - A renderer MAY retain its **rendered-output tree** (id → native element + computed layout) for drawing, hit-testing, and event routing — this is a cache of its own output, not state
 - The renderer MUST NOT retain component property values as business state, application control flow, or anything the application can change without emitting an opcode
 - The application owns the canonical retained UI tree
 - The engine emits **deltas only**; the renderer applies them to its native elements
 
 **Violation of this principle is a bug, not a feature.**
 
 ### Principle 2: Command-Based Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol transmits tree mutations as a stream of commands, NOT as serialized trees.**
 
 - Each frame is a **batch of delta commands** describing changes
 - Only **actual changes** are transmitted (diff-based reactive emission)
 - Protocol acts like a **VM instruction stream** / ABI
 - Deterministic, linear decoding without schema lookup or reflection
 
 ### Principle 3: Binary Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol MUST be binary.**
 
 - Open-source, cross-platform binary format
 - Fixed **16-byte instructions** in a ring buffer shared with the host via linear memory
 - Custom instruction-based bytecode, not schema-driven serialization
 - **Both directions are binary**: tree mutations (app → renderer) AND raw-input events (renderer → app) share the same instruction format, so the wire is language- and platform-agnostic

 ## Protocol Quick Reference
 
 The semantic surface is catalogued in the companion specs: **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`**
 (primitive views + component IDs), **`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** (core modifiers = the
 `PARAMETER` properties), **`spec/EVENTS.md`** (core events + listener bits),
 **`spec/LAYOUT.md`** (frame & layout allocation contract). The
 tables below are a quick recap of the protocol surface; the companion files
 carry the authoritative ID allocations.
 
 > **Implementation status lives in each project's `status.md`**, not in the
 > specs: `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/status.md`,
 > `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-gtk/status.md`,
 > `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/status.md`,
 > `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md`, `lib/java/pathland-render-html/status.md`,
 > and the other Rust crates' `status.md` files.
 
 ### Opcode Format
 
 Every opcode is exactly 16 bytes:
 
 ```
 [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
 ```
 
 See `spec/OPCODE.md` for the full format, ring buffer, arena, and frame lifecycle.
 
 ### Categories
 
 | Category | Value | Direction | Description |
 |----------|-------|-----------|-------------|
 | TREE | 0x01 | Guest → Host | Node create/delete/insert/remove/move |
 | PARAMETER | 0x02 | Guest → Host | Constraint properties (spacing, padding, …), design tokens |
 | EVENT | 0x03 | Host → Guest | Raw inputs: pointer down/move/up, key down/up |
 | META | 0x04 | Both | Reset, environment |
 
 ### Component Types (u16)
 
 Grouped ranges (see `spec/PRIMITIVES.md`):
 
 | Group | Component | ID |
 |-------|-----------|----|
 | **Primitive Drawing (0x01–0x0F)** | TEXT | 0x01 |
 | | IMAGE | 0x02 |
 | | COLOR | 0x03 |
 | | SHAPE | 0x04 |
 | | DIVIDER | 0x05 |
 | | SPACER | 0x06 |
 | | PROGRESS_VIEW | 0x07 |
 | | GAUGE | 0x08 |
 | | VIDEO (a `MEDIA_CONTROLLER`'s surface) | 0x0A |
 | **Layout & Container (0x10–0x1F)** | VSTACK | 0x10 |
 | | HSTACK | 0x11 |
