 ### Key Property IDs
 
 **Stack**: SPACING=0x0001, ALIGNMENT=0x0002, CONTENT_MARGINS=0x0005  
 **Text**: TEXT=0x000A, TEXT_ALIGNMENT=0x000C, LINE_LIMIT=0x000B, TRUNCATION_MODE=0x000D  
 **Style**: COLOR=0x100A, FONT_SIZE=0x1007, FONT_WEIGHT=0x1008, FONT_FAMILY=0x1009, BACKGROUND_COLOR=0x1001, BORDER_WIDTH=0x1003, BORDER_COLOR=0x1004, BORDER_RADIUS=0x1005, OPACITY=0x100D, VISIBLE=0x100E, Z_INDEX=0x100F, CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS=0x1010, PADDING=0x1011, PADDING_TOP/RIGHT/BOTTOM/LEFT=0x1012-0x1015  
 **Special**: WIDTH=0x100B (use -1=FILL, -2=HUG_CONTENT), HEIGHT=0x100C  
 **Semantic**: ROLE=0x2001, STATE=0x2002, ENABLED=0x2003, SELECTED=0x2004, EVENT_LISTENERS=0x2005 (u32 bitmask — which raw events a node wants reported), VALUE=0x2006, MIN_VALUE=0x2007, MAX_VALUE=0x2008, LABEL=0x200A, PROMPT=0x200B  
 **Binding/action**: ACTION_ID=0x2016, BINDING_ID=0x2017, TOGGLE_STYLE=0x2018 (Switch=0, Checkbox=1, Button=2)  
 **Media** (spec/MEDIA.md): MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID=0x103A (a `VIDEO`'s controller), MEDIA_SOURCE=0x103B, MEDIA_MUTED=0x103C, MEDIA_LOOP=0x103D, MEDIA_RATE=0x103E; PLAYBACK_STATE=0x1035 / MEDIA_POSITION=0x1036 / MEDIA_VOLUME=0x1037 live on the controller
 
 ### Colors
 
 - Literal colors are **sRGB** with D65 white point, packed as `0xAARRGGBB`
 - A color property may instead carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to a token path
 - Semantic token resolution and theme adaptation are **renderer-owned**
 
 ### Design Token System
 
 **Core Principle**: Application defines intent, overrides, and the theme.
 Renderer defines visual appearance, behavior, defaults, and interaction states.
 
 - The **application owns the theme**: token overrides (base = **light**, `dark.`-prefixed = **dark**) and token references in style properties. Token refs cover COLOR and non-color values (`Length` for spacing/padding/font size/radius/border/frame; `FontFamily.Token` for STRING) in the Rust and Java DSLs.
 - The **renderer owns** default token values (light + dark, the full Tier-1 catalog), token resolution (including explicit `dark.` = forced dark and parent fallback), effective color-scheme detection, interaction states (hover, pressed, focus, disabled), and theme adaptation
 - `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` identifies tokens by **dot-separated string paths** (e.g. `color.primary`, `space.2`) with the standard value-type encoding — there is no separate numeric tokenId system. A `dark.` prefix selects the dark variant (`dark.color.primary`); a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference whose path starts with `dark.` forces the dark value in either scheme
 - **Runtime theming**: `META::RESET_THEME` clears every app override; a replacement theme is reset + `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides in one frame. `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` forces `platform`/`light`/`dark`. Both are renderer state — no node is re-emitted. Java: `Emitter.replaceTheme`/`setColorScheme` + `PathlandSession.setTheme`/`setColorScheme`; Rust: `Engine::reset_theme`/`set_color_scheme`.
 - An unresolvable token reference leaves the property **unset** (renderer default), never an error or stale value.
 - The protocol MUST NEVER describe hover styles, click styles, visual transitions, conditional styling, or layout tuning for interaction states
 - **Deferred**: applying per-component tokens to native GTK/Qt leaf control chrome; web parent-path fallback.
 
 The HTML renderer's default token values are generated from `design/` (see
 "HTML base design" above). Full details: [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system)
 and the canonical catalog / color-scheme contract in [spec/TOKENS.md](./spec/TOKENS.md).
 
 ---
 
 ## Implementation Guidelines
 
 ### Adding New Component
 1. Add to `component_type` in `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Implement the component type in `pathland-core` (if it affects the retained tree)
 4. Implement native-element mapping in the target renderer (Goal 3–5)
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Adding New Property
 1. Add to the appropriate property module in `constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Handle the value type in `pathland-core`'s diff emission (if a stack/text/size property)
 4. Implement in each renderer's property application
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Modifying Protocol
 1. Update `spec/OPCODE.md` first (and `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` vectors)
 2. Update `constants.rs` and `pathland-core` encoding/emitters
 3. Verify backward compatibility; update `pathland-core`/`pathland-render-gtk` + tests
 4. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Changing the Wire Format
 - Bump the wire `version` field in `spec/OPCODE.md` and `pathland-core`'s header (currently 1). Pre-release format changes are acceptable while version stays 1.
 
 ### Keeping implementation status updated (MANDATORY)
 
 **The agent MUST keep the per-project `status.md` files in sync with the code.**
 Whenever you land a protocol or renderer change — a new component/property/
 command/event, a new encoder/decoder, a new widget mapping, a new modifier or
 renderer feature, a test that proves new surface — **update the affected
 project's `status.md`** (Implemented / Not implemented / gaps) in the same
 change. The specs (`spec/`) describe the protocol contract only and MUST NOT
 carry implementation status; status lives in `status.md` next to each
 implementing project.
 
 ---
 
 ## Common Pitfalls
 
 ### NEVER Do These
 | Anti-Pattern | Why Wrong | Correct |
 |--------------|-----------|---------|
 | Renderer stores application state | Violates statelessness | Application owns the tree |
 | Engine computes layout / emits rects | Violates declarative model | Emit structure + constraints; native elements lay out |
 | Send full trees | Inefficient | Diff-based reactive emission |
 | String property names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | String component names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | Generic RGB | Ambiguous | Explicitly sRGB |
 | Hover styles in protocol | Renderer job | Define in theme |
 | Heap allocation in steady-state emission | Slow | Preallocated snapshot slab + arena |
 
 ---
 
 ## Project Status
 
 **Complete**: 16-byte opcode engine (`pathland-core`), SwiftUI-style view DSL with decoupled chainable modifiers (`pathland-view`), declarative diff-based reactive emission (`pathland-core`), **reactive signals** (`pathland-core::signal` — writable `Signal` values bound to node text/properties, so a signal change re-emits only the bound nodes, reachable from Java via the `pathland_native_signal_*` / `node_bind_*` C ABI), host reader to a native-element description (`pathland-render-gtk`), opcode transport with network-batch encode/decode + time/size batching policy (`pathland-core-transport`), golden conformance vectors (incl. raw-input EVENT and network-batch bytes), typed raw-input event encode/decode, `no_std` builds, zero-alloc steady-state emission, the **bidirectional event ring** (host → guest EVENT opcodes in shared memory, drained by the host via a generic `pathland_native_drain_events` C ABI — the renderer only writes + wakes), the **GTK4 renderer** (`pathland-render-gtk`) with Rust demos that render through it without touching GTK directly, the **native Java library set** — `com.pathland.view` (open `View` interface + SwiftUI-like DSL, **Angular-parity signals/computed/effects** with synchronous flush, fine-grained emitter with **node-level binding effects**, `PLPL` wire codec, lazy **JNA ring interop** into `libpathland_core`, cross-platform `StateStore` + **`State`/`PersistentState`** auto-wired by the `pathland-view-processor` annotation processor), `com.pathland.render.html` (JNA shim over the Rust HTML renderer), `com.pathland.state.redis` (Lettuce `RedisStateStore`) — and the **Quarkus** (`pathland-quarkus-demo`) **and Spring Boot** (`pathland-spring-boot-demo`) **SSR + WebSocket demos**, both consuming the same shared views (`pathland-demo-views`) with per-window persisted `State` (Redis/in-memory — every browser window/tab gets its own UI model and state scope via a `sessionStorage` window id, so two windows never share a session). **`EVENT_LISTENERS`** (any element emits raw events via a u32 bitmask property) and **`onTapGesture`** (Rust + Java DSL modifier + app-side `TapRecognizer` over the raw pointer events). **Generic input routing** — the emitter returns tap-action / text-input / value-input registries (`RenderResult`), so the host forwards raw `EVENT` batches straight into the bound `State` signals and never reaches into a view's internals. **The media kit** (spec/MEDIA.md) — a non-visual `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` (0x30) state object owning a resource + transport as signals, referenced by a `VIDEO` (0x0A) surface and controlled by the app's own views; **audio has no view**. Implemented across spec, `pathland-core`, the GTK + HTML renderers, the TS DOM client, the Java DSL/emitter, and the Rust DSL/engine (a `MediaController` + `Video` + `attach()`, with string-property signal bindings and a **pinned** controller node id so a `SIZE_THAT_FITS` band swap never restarts playback). **Tests green across the workspace.**

 ---
 
 ## Quick Start
 
 1. Read this file and `spec/OPCODE.md`
 2. Run Rust tests: `cd lib/rust && cargo test` (runs all crates)
 3. Build/test the Java libraries: `cd lib/java && mvn install`
 4. Make small changes, verify they work
 
 ---
 
 ## Pathland Mindset
 
 **Always remember**:
 1. Protocol is King
 2. Renderers are Dumb (execute commands only)
 3. Applications are Smart (generate commands)
 4. Only Changes Matter (transmit mutations / reactive emission)
 5. Binary is Beautiful (efficient, deterministic)
 
 **When in doubt**: Check `spec/OPCODE.md`, the conformance vectors in `spec/CONFORMANCE.md`, and the companion catalogs (`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`, `spec/MODIFIERS.md`, `spec/EVENTS.md`, `spec/LAYOUT.md`), and the reference implementation (`pathland-core`). Ask: "Does this maintain stateless renderers?" "Does this only transmit actual changes?" "Does this describe WHAT the UI is, never WHERE?" "Is this representable as a 16-byte opcode in any language?"

 # HTML Base Design — Style Dictionary Plan
 
 **Status:** Complete
 **Branch:** `feature/design-system-style-dictionary`
 **Last updated:** October 28, 2026
 
 ---
 
 ## Goal
 
 Make the HTML renderer's base design a **CSS-first, Style Dictionary pipeline**:
 
 - Design tokens are authored in three layers (base → semantic → component).
 - Style Dictionary generates the token CSS.
 - The hand-authored reset and `.pathland-*` component CSS live in `design/html/` and consume
   the generated `var(--pl-*)` tokens.
 - The renderer embeds the generated bundle in Rust.
 - The design loop (edit tokens/CSS → rebuild CSS → preview) does not require changing Rust
   source files.
 
 ## Non-goals
 
 - **Multiple brands/themes.** Removed from scope.
 - **App-selected base designs, custom app base CSS, `BaseDesign`/`BaseDesignSource` APIs, and
   per-app `pathland.base-design.*` configuration.** Removed from scope. The HTML renderer has
   one built-in base design.
 - GTK/Qt renderer changes.
 - Generated Java/TypeScript token constants and documentation (possible follow-up).
-- A production hashed linked stylesheet (deferred; the renderer embeds the base CSS).
 - Any protocol change. `spec/TOKENS.md` remains the catalog contract.
 
 ---
 
 ## Architecture
 
 ### Three token layers
 
 | Layer | Contents | Emitted to CSS? | References |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | **base** | Palette (`base.color.blue.600`), spacing/type scales, radii, border widths, elevation primitives | No — resolved into literals | None |
 | **semantic** | `color.*`, `space.base`, `font.*`, `radius.*`, `border.width.*`, `elevation.*`, `control.*`, `size.control.*`, `opacity.disabled` | Yes | base |
 | **component** | `button.*`, `input.*`, `toggle.*`, `slider.*`, `progress.*`, `gauge.*`, `stepper.*`, `picker.*`, `menu.*`, `label.*`, `icon.*`, `spinner.*` | Yes | semantic (base only when no alias exists) |
 
 - Dark values use `$extensions.pathland.dark` on each token.
 - Base palette entries are distinct (`blue.600`, `blue.400`); semantic tokens explicitly
   reference the dark entry.
 - `space.<N>` remains generative: only `space.base` is emitted. Component dimensions reference
   the base scale (e.g. `base.space.3`), not the generative family.
 - `button.padding` becomes `button.padding.horizontal` / `.vertical`.
 - Internal component tokens (durations, z-index, `em` icon sizes) are emitted but are
   renderer-internal, not part of `spec/TOKENS.md`.
 
 ### Source and generated files
 
 ```
 design/
   package.json                  # style-dictionary v5, chokidar; scripts: build/dev/check
   package-lock.json
   style-dictionary.config.mjs
   tokens/
     base/*.tokens.json          # internal palette + scales
     semantic/*.tokens.json      # catalog semantic + shared control.*
     component/*.tokens.json     # full per-component token surface
   html/
     reset.css                   # preflight + html/body
     components.css              # .pathland-* rules, consuming var(--pl-*)
   scripts/
     build.mjs                   # SD build + concat reset+tokens+components
     dev.mjs                     # build + watch tokens + html/*.css
     check.mjs                   # layer/catalog/type/reference validation
   build/                        # generated, gitignored
     tokens.css
     base.css
     manifest.json
   README.md
 lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/base.css   # synced generated bundle (committed)
 scripts/sync-design-css.sh
 ```
 
 ### Renderer embedding
 
 ```rust
 // lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/src/css.rs
 const CSS: &str = include_str!("../assets/base.css");
 pub fn builtin_css() -> &'static str { CSS }
 pub const STYLE: &str = concat!("<style>", include_str!("../assets/base.css"), "</style>");
 ```
 
 - `render_document` keeps using `css::STYLE`.
 - The synced crate copy is generated from `design/build/base.css` and committed for packaging.
 - `scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check` fails on drift.
 - The renderer remains stateless and a pure function of the opcode stream; the base design is
   compiled in.
 
 ### Style Dictionary configuration
 
 - Style Dictionary v5, Node ≥22, DTCG (`$value`, `$type`, `$description`, `$extensions`).
 - Custom formats:
   - `pathland/css-tokens` emits:
     - `:root` semantic + component variables;
     - `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` dark layer;
     - `:root[data-pathland-scheme='dark']` and `:root[data-pathland-scheme='light']`;
     - `:root` forced-dark `--pl-dark-*` variables.
   - `pathland/manifest` emits `{ path, layer, type, cssVar, darkCssVar, internal }` for
     validation and future codegen.
 - Reference rules:
   - semantic/component → emitted token: `var(--pl-<target>)` (light/dark) and
     `var(--pl-dark-<target>)` (forced-dark);
   - → base token: resolved literal;
   - no explicit dark value: reference the emitted target so its dark layer wins;
   - explicit dark extension: use it for the dark and forced-dark layers.
 - Base tokens are filtered from the CSS output.
 - Dimensions preserve the current `px`/`rem` values.
 
 > **Implementation note (landed):** token files use **flat DTCG keys** carrying
 > their dotted path rather than nested groups. The Pathland catalog contains
 > paths that are both a leaf and a group (`control.border` is a color while
 > `control.border.width` is a dimension), which nested DTCG trees cannot
 > represent; Style Dictionary's custom formats read and resolve the flat maps
 > directly (see `design/scripts/token-model.mjs`).
 
 ---
 
 ## Phases
 
 ### Phase 1 — Extract the hand-authored CSS
 
 **Deliverables**
 
 - `design/html/reset.css` — preflight + `html`/`body` from `css.rs`, preserving the Tailwind
   MIT attribution.
 - `design/html/components.css` — every `.pathland-*` rule moved verbatim.
 - `design/html/tokens.css` — temporary hand-authored copy of the current token block
   (`:root`, dark media, forced-dark).
 - `scripts/sync-design-css.sh` — copy the three files to
   `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/`; `--check` mode.
 - `css.rs` assembles the synced files with `include_str!`/`concat!`; output unchanged.
 - Wire the sync into `scripts/lib.sh` (`build_rust_html`), the `refresh-ide` Maven profile,
   and CI.
 
 **Verification**

 - `cargo test -p pathland-html-golden`.
 - `scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check`.
 - Rendered output is textually unchanged.
 
 ### Phase 2 — Style Dictionary pipeline for the existing token surface

 ### Phase 3 — Full component token layer
 
 **Deliverables**

   CSS.

 - **base** tokens are literals. They are internal: the generator resolves them
   to literals and **never emits them** as CSS variables. Override the semantic
   or component token instead.
 - **semantic** tokens reference base tokens. They are the protocol catalog
   surface (`spec/TOKENS.md`).
 - **component** tokens reference semantic tokens, or a base scale token
   (`base.space.*`, `base.radius.*`, `base.border.width.*`, `base.size.*`,
   `base.font.*`) when no semantic alias exists. A component token that must
   reference a base **color** needs an explicit justification:
 
   ```json
   "$extensions": {
     "pathland": { "baseReference": "why this base color is used directly" }
   }
   ```
 
 ### Dark values
 
 Dark values live on `$extensions.pathland.dark`:
 
 ```json
 {
   "color.primary": {
     "$value": "{base.color.blue.600}",
     "$type": "color",
     "$extensions": { "pathland": { "dark": "{base.color.blue.400}" } }
   }
 }
 ```
 
 The generator emits four token layers:
 
 1. `:root` (light),
 2. `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) :root:not([data-pathland-scheme])`,
 3. `:root[data-pathland-scheme='dark']` (forced dark) and
    `:root[data-pathland-scheme='light']` (forced light),
 4. the forced-dark variable family `--pl-dark-*` for explicit `dark.` token
    references.
 
 A reference to another **emitted** token compiles to `var(--pl-<target>)` (and
 `var(--pl-dark-<target>)` in the forced-dark family), so the target's dark layer
 wins. A reference to a **base** token compiles to its literal. With no explicit
 dark value, the dark layers reference the same target variable.
 
 ### Internal tokens
 
 Durations, z-index, and `em` icon sizes are renderer-internal (not part of
 `spec/TOKENS.md`). Mark them with `$extensions.pathland.internal: true`; they are
 still emitted and listed in `build/manifest.json` with `"internal": true`.
 
 ## Validation
 
 `npm run check` enforces:
 
 - every Tier-1 token in `pathland_core::TIER1_TOKENS` is present;
 - layer direction (semantic → base, component → semantic/base scale) and
   no unresolved references;
 - every emitted token has light, platform-dark, forced-dark-scheme, and
   forced-dark variable declarations;
 - every `$type: dimension` token is recognized by the canonical
   `isLengthToken` rules in `pathland-render-html::token_spec` (add a rule there
   when introducing a new dimension path);
 - durations / z-index / icon sizes are marked internal;
 - `build/manifest.json` and `build/tokens.css` match the current sources, and
-  base tokens are not emitted.
+  base tokens are not emitted;
+- `build/base.css.name` matches the SHA-256 of `build/base.css`.
 
+## Serving the stylesheet
+
+The renderer supports two deliveries:
+
+- **inline** (the library default, `render_document` / `render`): the whole
+  base design is a `<style>` block in the document head;
+- **linked** (`render_document_linked` / Java `renderLinked`): an external
+  `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{base}/base-<hash>.css">`. Token overrides
+  (`<style data-pathland-tokens>`) and fit-band rules stay inline after it.
+
+The Spring Boot and Quarkus SSR starters use the linked form and serve the
+renderer-owned bytes at `{base}/base-<hash>.css` (global and per-app bases) with
+`Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. A new design build gets a
+new hash, so the URL busts the cache. Library hosts can keep the inline default
+or serve `baseCss()` / `baseCssName()` themselves.
+
 ## Preview
 
 `preview/index.html` loads `build/base.css` and renders representative
 `.pathland-*` markup (buttons, fields, toggles, slider, progress, stepper, menu,
 media) with a light/dark/system switcher. Run `npm run dev -- --serve` and open
 <http://127.0.0.1:4173/>. This is a development tool, not an app-selectable base
 design.
 
 ## Generated files — do not edit
 
 - `build/tokens.css`
 - `build/manifest.json`
 - `build/base.css`
+- `build/base.css.name`
 - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/base.css` (synced copy)
+- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/base.css.name` (synced copy)
 
 Edit the token files or `html/{reset,components}.css`, then rebuild and sync.

state.output:
# pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 2, 2026

The **Java binding to the Rust HTML renderer** (`dev.pathland.render.html`) — a
thin **JNA shim** over `libpathland_render_html`. There is a **single renderer**
(the Rust crate), reused by every language; the former hand-written retained
Java renderer is removed. Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Stateless JNA shim**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` links the Rust cdylib;
  `render(frame, root)` / `renderFragment(frame, root)` /
  `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a self-contained snapshot frame to
  HTML in one pass (no retained tree, no `applyFrame`); `pathland_html_free`
  releases native strings. Lazy-loaded; skipped (test assumption) when the dylib
  is absent from `java.library.path`.
- **Debug comments**: `renderDebug(frame, root)` / `renderFragmentDebug(...)`
  bind the Rust `pathland_html_render_debug` exports — each rendered node is
  prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component type and the modifiers
  applied (opt-in; the plain `render` output is unchanged).
- **Full Rust renderer surface** (canonical): all spec components render inline
  (structural + decorative CSS in a single `style` attribute), ARIA/event
  attributes, `IS_SECURE` → password, `TOGGLE_STYLE` variants,
  `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, and literal colors inline. The renderer injects its own
  built-in `<style>` block (preflight reset + design tokens + `.pathland-*`
  component defaults) into every document — no external CSS, no `/tailwind.css`.
- **Icon glyphs from the shared renderer**: `iconSvg(String name)` binds the
  Rust `pathland_html_icon_svg` export over the C ABI — the full inline `<svg>`
  for a canonical `ICON_NAME` (unknown/extension names → the renderer's
  fallback glyph, never null). Hosts serve `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from
  it (Spring/Quarkus route a few lines in their starters), so the DOM client's
  lazy icon fetch gets the same glyph data SSR inlines from — one Rust source,
  no per-platform static icon files. `HtmlRendererTest` covers it.
- **Demos use the shim**: `SessionApp` no longer calls `applyFrame`; SSR renders
  the mount frame through `HtmlRenderer.render(sink.frame(), rootId)`. The
  renderer is compiled once at startup.
- **Text fields share one component class**: `TEXT_FIELD` inputs and `TEXT_EDITOR`
  textareas render with `class="pathland-input"` (Tailwind-style inset-outline
  styling from the Rust renderer's CSS); the copied `@pathland/dom-renderer`
  bundle (content-hashed `dom-renderer-<sha256>.js` in both demos) mirrors the
  class so delta-created fields hydrate identically.

## Removed (September 2026)

- `compileTailwind(overrideCss)` and the `pathland_tailwind_compile` binding are
  **deleted** — the renderer is inline-only now and needs no compiler. The demo
  `/tailwind.css` endpoints (`TailwindCssController` / `TailwindCssResource`)
  and the `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/tailwind.css">` in both `SessionApp`
  files are removed.

## Not implemented / gaps

- **Typography uses the platform system font stack** (`system-ui,
  -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, …`) — the Rust renderer's document head
  makes no external/webfont requests, so the demo pages render without loading
  any font files and work offline. An app can still override `font.body.family`
  via a `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` to any font it hosts.
- The shim is unaffected by the Rust renderer's September 2026 shell alignment
  (SPACER/MENU/STEPPER/GAUGE/PICKER markup now matches the DOM client's runtime
  shells); the demos' SSR output reflects the Rust renderer as-is, pinned by the
  `pathland-html-golden` conformance harness. `HtmlRendererTest` covers the
  semantic-role → element mapping (`NAVIGATION`→`<nav>`, `HEADER`→`<h2>`,
  `TEXT_STYLE` headings) and the DSL's rejection of non-semantic role codes,
  plus media rendering (a `VIDEO` surface bound to its `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` —
  native `<video controls>` + `data-pathland-controller`, the non-visual hidden
  controller shell, image `alt` from the accessibility label,
  `ContentMode Fill`→`cover`).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-render-html` — JNA shim tests (skip when the Rust dylib
is absent); part of the non-demo reactor run on JDK 17.

# pathland-spring-boot-starter — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 3, 2026

Spring Boot auto-configuration for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each
app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding the starter dependency + a
`PathlandApp` bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at their own
subpaths (the BFF layout).

## Implemented

- **`PathlandAutoConfiguration`** (`@AutoConfiguration`, `@EnableWebSocket` since Spring
  Boot 3.5 no longer auto-enables it) + `META-INF/spring/…/AutoConfiguration.imports`:
  - default `StateStore` bean (`@ConditionalOnMissingBean` — Redis-or-in-memory),
  - `PathlandHost` bean (shut down with the context): every `MountedApp` bean plus the
    lone `PathlandApp` bean mounted at `/` (unless an explicit `MountedApp` claims the
    root). Without any app the host is empty and the starter is inert.
  - a `WebSocketConfigurer` registering **one handler per app** at its framework base
    (`/_pathland/ws` for the root, `/{mount}/_pathland/ws` otherwise). Each connection
    gets a fresh `uiId` (its UI model) + the client's `wid` (per-window state scope)
    from the WS `?wid=` query param (kept in `sessionStorage`, never in the page URL),
  - `PathlandIndexController` (SSR catch-all dispatching to the longest-mount app with
    the prefix stripped + a framework static controller serving the bundle + asset mount
    from `classpath:/static/_pathland/**` at both `/_pathland/**` and `/{app}/_pathland/**`;
    the more-specific mapping beats `/{*path}`, and the `!Upgrade` header excludes WS).
    When no static file matches an `/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg` request, the controller
    serves the renderer-owned glyph from the shared Rust renderer
    (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` → `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache header —
    no static icon files on any host, and a host can still override a glyph with a file.
    The framework controller honors byte-range requests (`206 Partial Content` +
    `Content-Range`, `416` for unsatisfiable ranges, `Accept-Ranges` on the full
    response) — a `<video>` (a `MediaController`'s playback) seeking beyond its
    buffer issues a `Range`
    request, and answering it with a full `200` would make browsers restart the media
    at byte 0.
    SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS).
- **SSR debug comments**: the host reads the `pathland.debug-html` property
  (`@Value("${pathland.debug-html:false}")`) and forwards it to each registry, enabling
  per-node HTML comments in SSR output when set.
- **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `pathland.service-worker`
  (default `false`) forwards to the host; the SSR emits `data-pathland-service-worker`
  and the controller serves `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` +
  `Cache-Control: no-cache` (a stable, uncached script the browser byte-compares).
- **`SpringConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketSession` to `PathlandConnection`.
  `AutoCloseable`: a failed send surfaces as a close (the session's
  `closeConnection` closes the underlying session) so the DOM client reconnects +
  `META::RESYNC` instead of silently stalling on an open socket.
- **Heartbeat** — the socket replies to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
  **at the transport layer** (through its `SpringConnection`, no actor/session
  dependency; spec/OPCODE.md §Transport heartbeat).
- **Observability (issue #62)** — `spring-boot-starter-actuator` supplies the
  `MeterRegistry`; auto-config builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over it (decorated with
  `TracingTelemetry` when an `OpenTelemetry` bean is present — add
  `micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel` to opt in) and a `HealthIndicator` reporting the host
  UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/actuator/health`. The `pathland.*` meters are
  exposed at `/actuator/prometheus` (add `micrometer-registry-prometheus`).

## App DX

```java
@SpringBootApplication
public class MyApp {
    public static void main(String[] args) { SpringApplication.run(MyApp.class, args); }
    @Bean PathlandApp pathlandApp() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); }
    @Bean MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); } // optional 2nd app
}
```

## Verified by

`mvn test` — `PathlandAutoConfigurationTest` (`@SpringBootTest`): a `PathlandApp` bean
mounts at `/` and SSR renders the root. `MultiSessionWebSocketTest`
(`@SpringBootTest(RANDOM_PORT)`) opens **100 concurrent real WS sessions** against
`/_pathland/ws` (via the shared `pathland-server-core` test-jar probe) and asserts each
connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level PONGs, stays isolated, and is never closed by
the peer. `PathlandObservabilityTest` (`@SpringBootTest` + `MockMvc`) asserts
`/actuator/health` reports the `pathland` component UP and the auto-configured
`PathlandTelemetry` is a `MicrometerTelemetry` registering `pathland.*` meters.
Manual: the `pathland-spring-boot-demo` renders `/`, `/kitchen`, `/settings`
and the 404 fallback **and a second app at `/app2`**; a WebSocket handshake to
`/_pathland/ws` and `/app2/_pathland/ws` returns 101.=== QUARKUS ===
# pathland-quarkus-starter — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 17, 2026

Quarkus integration for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each app's reserved
`/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding the starter dependency + a `PathlandApp` CDI
bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at their own subpaths
(the BFF layout).

## Implemented

- **`PathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/_pathland/ws")` for the root app: 1:1 sessions
  per connection (a fresh `uiId` per connection + the client's `wid` state scope from
  the `?wid=` query param), binary events routed into the root registry of the
  `PathlandHost`. **Stateless (critical)**: quarkus-websockets-next endpoints default
  to `@Singleton` — one shared instance for all connections — so the per-connection
  ids come from `connection.id()` + the handshake and the `QuarkusConnection` adapters
  live in a map keyed by connection id. Memoizing `uiId`/`wid`/`transport` on the
  shared instance collapsed every connection onto ONE session (multiple browsers shared
  one UI model — a probe or second tab drove the first tab's session).
- **`MountedPathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/{app}/_pathland/ws")` for mounted apps:
  the `{app}` path param resolves the app's registry. Mount paths are single-segment.
  Same stateless rule as the root socket.
- **`IndexResource`** — JAX-RS SSR catch-all (`/` + deep links; `/_pathland/**` and the
  Quarkus non-application root `/q/**` — health/metrics — excluded via negative lookahead)
  dispatching to the longest-mount app (prefix stripped);
  SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS);
  per-app framework files (`/{app}/_pathland/...`, e.g. the mounted app's bundle) are
  served from the shared `/_pathland/**` classpath mount. Quarkus serves the global
  `/_pathland/**` bundle + asset mount from `META-INF/resources` before JAX-RS.
  **`/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg`** (global base JAX-RS route + the mounted-base
  `frameworkFile` path) serves the renderer-owned icon glyphs from the shared
  Rust renderer (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` → `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an
  `immutable` cache header — no static icon files on any host.
- **`PathlandRegistryProducer`** — CDI `@Produces @Singleton` `PathlandHost` from every
  `MountedApp` bean plus the lone `PathlandApp` bean (mounted at `/`); `@Disposes` shuts
  it down. Reads the `pathland.debug-html` config property (default `false`) to enable
  per-node HTML comments in SSR output, and `pathland.service-worker` (default `false`)
  to opt the DOM client into the per-window-id service worker (issue #155) — served at
  `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
- **`ServiceWorkerFilter`** — serves `/_pathland/sw.js` (root and mounted bases) with
  `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so the client's root-scoped
  registration succeeds. A `Filters` handler always runs before routes, so it wins over
  Quarkus's static-resource handler (which sends neither header, and whose configured
  max-age would otherwise cache the script and delay update detection).
- **Observability (issue #62)** — `quarkus-micrometer` (a `MeterRegistry` bean) +
  `quarkus-smallrye-health`: the producer builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over the
  registry and decorates it with `TracingTelemetry` when a `Tracer` bean is present and
  `quarkus.otel.enabled` (default `true`; the starter never touches the OTel API when
  the extension is absent/disabled). `PathlandHealthCheck` (`@Readiness`) reports the
  host UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/q/health`; the `pathland.*` meters appear
  at `/q/metrics`.
- **`QuarkusConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketConnection` to `PathlandConnection`.
  Sends are **serialized** (one `sendBinary` subscription in flight, the rest queued),
  and a **send failure closes the connection** so the session drops it and the DOM
  client reconnects + `META::RESYNC` (recoverable) instead of silently stalling on an
  "open" socket that never delivers (the remote seekbar symptom). **Send timeout**: a
  `sendBinary` that neither completes nor fails within 10 s (a half-dead connection /
  a dropped proxy upstream leg) is marked failed and closed — a hung send would
  otherwise wedge the serialized drain forever. **Keep-alive pings**: the connection
  sends a WS-protocol ping every 15 s (browsers auto-pong) to keep the connection warm
  through middleboxes and detect a dead client; `close()` stops the keep-alive
  scheduler (the sockets' `@OnClose` calls it).
- **Heartbeat** — both sockets reply to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
  **at the transport layer** (through their `QuarkusConnection`, no actor/session
  dependency, and a PING never creates or wakes a session); spec/OPCODE.md
  §Transport heartbeat.
- **Failure handling** — `fail()` logs the reason; `close()` (socket `@OnClose`)
  no longer calls `close()` on the already-closed connection (no spurious
  "Connection already closed" noise). A **transient write failure on a connection
  that still reports open is logged, not closed** — only a confirmed-dead channel
  (or a send hung past the timeout) warrants closing. The send-timeout task is
  **cancelled when the send completes**, so a completed-but-late callback can't
  false-time-out and kill a healthy connection. Keep-alive pings are sent directly
  (Vert.x serializes writes — no sync with `sendBinary` needed).
- `META-INF/beans.xml` so Quarkus discovers the starter.

## App DX

```java
@ApplicationScoped
public class MyApp {
    @Produces @Singleton PathlandApp main() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); }
    @Produces @Singleton MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); }
}
```

## Verified by

Manual: the `pathland-quarkus-demo` renders `/` (the music player, whose Now
Playing pane embeds the small `/ad` app via a **same-server `ProxyView`**,
spec/PROXY.md) and `/ad` (the ad app); a WebSocket handshake to `/_pathland/ws`
and `/ad/_pathland/ws` returns 101. `ProxyDemoTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts
`GET /` embeds the `/ad` app's subtree with remapped node ids
(`data-pathland-id="1073741825"` — proxy block 0 + origin id 1). Core behavior is
covered by `pathland-server-core` tests. `MultiSessionWebSocketTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) opens **100 concurrent real WS
sessions** against `/_pathland/ws` (via the shared `pathland-server-core` test-jar
probe) and asserts each connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level PONGs, stays isolated,
and is never closed by the peer.
`PathlandObservabilityTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts `/q/health` reports the Pathland
check UP and `/q/metrics` exposes the `pathland.*` namespace.

state.output:
# Pathland base design

The built-in look of the HTML renderer, generated from a **three-layer Style
Dictionary pipeline** plus hand-authored reset/component CSS.

```
tokens/base/*.tokens.json        internal palette + scales          (not emitted)
tokens/semantic/*.tokens.json    protocol catalog semantics        (emitted)
tokens/component/*.tokens.json   per-component surface             (emitted)
html/reset.css                   Tailwind-derived preflight        (hand-authored)
html/components.css              .pathland-* rules                 (hand-authored)
```

The generated bundle is `build/base.css` (reset + `tokens.css` + components).
`lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/base.css` is the synced, committed
copy the renderer embeds with `include_str!`; the renderer has one built-in base
design and no app-facing design selection.

## Commands

```sh
npm --prefix design ci          # install (CI / clean checkout)
npm --prefix design run build   # Style Dictionary + build/base.css
npm --prefix design run check   # catalog/layer/dark/dimension validation
npm --prefix design run dev     # rebuild on token/CSS changes
npm --prefix design run dev -- --serve   # also serve preview/ on :4173
scripts/sync-design-css.sh      # copy build/base.css into the Rust crate
scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check
```

After changing tokens or CSS: `npm --prefix design run build`, then
`scripts/sync-design-css.sh`, then run `cargo test -p pathland-render-html`.

`build/` and `node_modules/` are gitignored. `package-lock.json` is committed.

## Tokens

Each token is a flat DTCG entry: `$value`, `$type`, optional `$description` and
`$extensions.pathland`. Keys carry their full dotted path because the catalog
contains paths that are both a leaf and a group (`control.border` is a color,
`control.border.width` is a dimension), which nested DTCG trees cannot represent.

- **base** tokens are literals. They are internal: the generator resolves them
  to literals and **never emits them** as CSS variables. Override the semantic
  or component token instead.
- **semantic** tokens reference base tokens. They are the protocol catalog
  surface (`spec/TOKENS.md`).
- **component** tokens reference semantic tokens, or a base scale token
  (`base.space.*`, `base.radius.*`, `base.border.width.*`, `base.size.*`,
  `base.font.*`) when no semantic alias exists. A component token that must
  reference a base **color** needs an explicit justification:

  ```json
  "$extensions": {
    "pathland": { "baseReference": "why this base color is used directly" }
  }
  ```

### Dark values

Dark values live on `$extensions.pathland.dark`:

```json
{
  "color.primary": {
    "$value": "{base.color.blue.600}",
    "$type": "color",
    "$extensions": { "pathland": { "dark": "{base.color.blue.400}" } }
  }
}
```

The generator emits four token layers:

1. `:root` (light),
2. `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) :root:not([data-pathland-scheme])`,
3. `:root[data-pathland-scheme='dark']` (forced dark) and
   `:root[data-pathland-scheme='light']` (forced light),
4. the forced-dark variable family `--pl-dark-*` for explicit `dark.` token
   references.

A reference to another **emitted** token compiles to `var(--pl-<target>)` (and
`var(--pl-dark-<target>)` in the forced-dark family), so the target's dark layer
wins. A reference to a **base** token compiles to its literal. With no explicit
dark value, the dark layers reference the same target variable.

### Internal tokens

Durations, z-index, and `em` icon sizes are renderer-internal (not part of
`spec/TOKENS.md`). Mark them with `$extensions.pathland.internal: true`; they are
still emitted and listed in `build/manifest.json` with `"internal": true`.

## Validation

`npm run check` enforces:

- every Tier-1 token in `pathland_core::TIER1_TOKENS` is present;
- layer direction (semantic → base, component → semantic/base scale) and
  no unresolved references;
- every emitted token has light, platform-dark, forced-dark-scheme, and
  forced-dark variable declarations;
- every `$type: dimension` token is recognized by the canonical
  `isLengthToken` rules in `pathland-render-html::token_spec` (add a rule there
  when introducing a new dimension path);
- durations / z-index / icon sizes are marked internal;
- `build/manifest.json` and `build/tokens.css` match the current sources, and
  base tokens are not emitted.

## Preview

`preview/index.html` loads `build/base.css` and renders representative
`.pathland-*` markup (buttons, fields, toggles, slider, progress, stepper, menu,
media) with a light/dark/system switcher. Run `npm run dev -- --serve` and open
<http://127.0.0.1:4173/>. This is a development tool, not an app-selectable base
design.

## Generated files — do not edit

- `build/tokens.css`
- `build/manifest.json`
- `build/base.css`
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/base.css` (synced copy)

Edit the token files or `html/{reset,components}.css`, then rebuild and sync.

state.output:
- **SSR debug comments (property-gated)**: `PathlandSession`/`PathlandRegistry` take a
  `debugHtml` flag (constructor + `isDebugHtml()`); when set, `renderHtml` uses the
  renderer's debug mode so every rendered node is prefixed with an HTML comment naming
  its component and the modifiers applied. The Spring/Quarkus starters bind it to the
  `pathland.debug-html` property (default `false`).
- **Reserved framework root**: `PathlandSession.PATHLAND_BASE` (`/_pathland`) — the
  SSR page carries the app's base as `data-pathland-base` and the DOM-client bundle is
  injected at `{base}/dom-renderer-<sha256>.js` (`PathlandAssets` reads the current
  name from the `_pathland/dom-renderer.current` manifest on the classpath, falling
  back to the literal `dom-renderer.js` when absent) so the client's WebSocket and
  asset refs resolve from the same reserved prefix (spec DSL.md). The content-hashed
  name busts the immutable asset cache with a fresh URL per build. Multi-app hosts
  give each mount its own base.
- **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `PathlandHost` carries a
  host-level `serviceWorker` flag (default `false`; one registration covers the
  whole origin) threaded to every `PathlandRegistry`; `PathlandSession.renderHtml`
  emits `data-pathland-service-worker="true"` on `<html>` when set, and the DOM
  client registers `{base}/sw.js` (root scope) / unregisters when absent (the kill
  switch). `PathlandRegistry.serviceWorkerUrl()` names the served script.
  `renderHtml` also emits `data-pathland-ssr-scoped="true"` when the request carried
  a real per-window id, so the client can skip its initial `META::RESYNC` (the SSR
  was already rendered with that window's state and the live session shares it).
